# ADVISOR: everything in one file

> ADVISOR is an MCP server for the Wayne State app stack. Your coding agent asks it about our standards, supported versions, docs and checks, and it answers read-only from the stack's own files.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/README.md

## ADVISOR

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static field map of the stack (open it in a browser).

On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Documentation: the full docs live at [`site/docs/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/site/docs/index.html), built from `docs/` by the shared docs builder (`composer docs`). The docs wear the front page's look through the builder's `theme` key in `docs/docs.json`: [`docs/_header.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/docs/_header.html) is the sheet head every docs page gets (keep its links in step with the front page's), and [`docs/theme/advisor.css`](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/docs/theme/advisor.css) holds the paper, Fraunces titles, code ground, callouts and the derived dark mode; the build copies it to `site/docs/theme/`. Edit those two files, never `site/assets/docs.css` or `docs.js` (Squire's kit), then run `composer docs`. The back of the map, now with the same legend as the front.

### Where the code lives

The canonical repository is [enterprise-apps/advisor](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/advisor) on git.wayne.edu: clone it over SSH as `git@git.wayne.edu:enterprise-apps/advisor.git`, or over HTTPS as `https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/advisor.git`. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are made there, by the maintainer, with an approver. CI runs on git.wayne.edu, on its instance runner.

GitHub ([waynestate/advisor](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor)) is a read-only push mirror of it: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it.

An advisor with office hours in two buildings is just hard to find. Ours keeps one office: git.wayne.edu.

> Every WSU student has an advisor. Now every WSU app does too, and this one answers email.

ADVISOR is an MCP server for the Wayne State application stack, a bit like Laravel Boost but for WSU. It orients a
developer who is new to the stack and gives their coding agent nine read-only tools into it: the CREED standards and
policy, PROCTOR results, the upgrade path, the WayneUI markup contract and migration guide, SESAME and HELMET
guidance, and the parts list.
Ask it "which PHP can I build on?" and it answers from the policy file, with the date and the source, instead of from
whatever the model remembers.

It is read-only. It cannot write a file, run a shell command, or call out to the network. The two things it
can start are the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor` and Booster's read-only `plan`, both with a fixed argument shape.

### Where it sits in WELD

The stack is the Wayne State application stack. WELD, Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed, is its Laravel starter app.
You can add ADVISOR to a WELD app or to any other Wayne State PHP app, and in either case it is the part of the stack
that talks to your coding agent.

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| **WayneUI** | interface (project 0) |
| **CREED** | version policy and written standards |
| **PROCTOR** | checks an app |
| **SESAME** | sign-in inside the app |
| **HELMET** | runtime baseline |
| **Sourdough** | starter |
| **Preflight** | CI components |
| **Pinstripe** | coding standard |
| **Booster** | upgrades |
| **Rollcall** | fleet census |
| **Drawbridge** | sign-in gateway |
| **Squire** | deploy kit |
| **Parity** | Citadel on your computer |
| **ADVISOR** | MCP server |
| **WELD** | the Laravel starter app |

ADVISOR serves a bundled copy of what these projects publish (see "Served content"), so it works offline, and it does
not replace Laravel Boost. Boost knows Laravel; ADVISOR knows WSU. Run both.

### Install

PHP 8.3 or newer (8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 are tested). Add it to the app as a dev dependency:

```
composer require --dev waynestate/advisor
```

The command is then `php vendor/bin/advisor`. This works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, because it is one PHP
command and not a shell script.

ADVISOR is on Packagist: `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.3`. No extra repository needed.

### Quick start

1. Print the config your MCP client needs, and read it:

   ```
   php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude
   ```

2. Write it into the project when you are happy with it:

   ```
   php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
   ```

3. Open the project in your client and approve the `advisor` server by name when it asks.

The command it registers is always the same fixed string, `php vendor/bin/advisor mcp`, with `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in
its environment. Clients: `claude` (`.mcp.json`), `warriorgpt` (`.mcp.json`), `cursor` (`.cursor/mcp.json`), `vscode`
(`.vscode/mcp.json`) and `codex` (TOML, printed only; paste it into `~/.codex/config.toml`).

#### One line for Claude Code

If you would rather type it than generate it, this does the same as `install --client=claude --write`; project scope
keeps it out of your other projects, and the same "do not commit it" warning applies:

```
claude mcp add --scope project advisor -e ADVISOR_ENABLED=1 -- php vendor/bin/advisor mcp
```

#### No PHP on your PATH? Use Docker

If PHP is not on your PATH, point the client at Docker instead. Run it from the project root, the folder that holds
`vendor/`, with a hand-written `.mcp.json` like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "advisor": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "-i",
        "--rm",
        "--network",
        "none",
        "-v",
        ".:/app:ro",
        "-w",
        "/app",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_ENABLED=1",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT=/app",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_READ_ONLY=1",
        "composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0",
        "php",
        "vendor/bin/advisor",
        "mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The container has no network, and the project is mounted read-only. `ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack` keeps the tools that start
programs (proctor, upgrade_path) off, because those need the app's own PHP. Some clients want an absolute path in
place of `.` for the mount; give them one. Advice comes in; nothing goes out. This file is written by hand, so keep it
out of git like the generated one.

`install` never replaces a different existing `advisor` entry unless you pass `--force`, keeps your other servers, and
warns when the file is not in `.gitignore`. A client config starts a program on whoever opens the project, so do not
commit a generated one; this repository ignores `.mcp.json` for that reason.

Run the client from the folder that holds `vendor/`. If it starts somewhere else, set `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT`.

#### Laravel apps

ADVISOR also ships a Laravel adapter on `laravel/mcp`, auto-discovered by the service provider. With it, the same
server runs as `php artisan mcp:start advisor`, beside Boost. Publish the config if you want it in the app:

```
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=advisor-config
```

Settings come from the same `ADVISOR_*` variables, read through `config/advisor.php`. The same rules apply: off unless
`ADVISOR_ENABLED` is set, and never in production.

### What it offers

Nine tools, all read-only. Each one says where its answer came from:

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `list_projects` | The stack's projects, WayneUI first, with built or proposed state, package and version. |
| `get_project_status` | One project: state, package, version, PHP constraint, its floor under today's policy, next step. |
| `read_project_docs` | A project's README, best practices, or (WayneUI only) markup contract and 1.x to 2.x migration guide, paged. |
| `policy_lookup` | Support state for a runtime or tool (and an optional version) from CREED, as of today, worked out by CREED's own reader (`waynestate/creed`), the one PROCTOR carries a copy of. A version older than every one the policy lists is answered as end of life, with a note. |
| `list_stack_rules` | CREED handbook rules, each with its file and line, filtered by app permutation and chapter. |
| `owner_of` | Answers "which project owns X?" from the bundled ownership table, built from the stack's one-owner-per-rule decision first: the owner, its role, the projects around it, and the decision each answer comes from. Pass a topic or the whole question ("who owns composer audit"). |
| `playbook_lookup` | A shared value by key, or every key: an environment variable of the same name wins, then Playbook; secret-looking keys are refused. |
| `run_proctor_check` | Runs the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor check` against the bundled policy and returns the findings. |
| `upgrade_path` | Plans the app's PHP and/or Laravel upgrade, one supported hop at a time, via Booster's read-only `plan`. Inputs: from_php (the version the app runs today, when the project names none), to_php, to_laravel. |

The groups split by what they may start: `stack` never starts a program, `proctor` starts the app's own
`vendor/bin/proctor`, and `booster` starts Booster's read-only `plan` (never `run`). Set `ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack`
when you want ADVISOR as pure reference material.

| Resource | Serves |
|---|---|
| `advisor://policy` | CREED's policy file. |
| `advisor://creed/` | One per handbook chapter. |
| `advisor://guide/` | Hand-written guides; the first is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel". |

Prompts: `orient_me` and `plan_upgrade`.

Here is what that looks like when you ask. Each numbered control point is one of the tools above, with the arguments the
front page's own route table sends:

Everything ADVISOR returns is labeled as reference data. PROCTOR in CI, not ADVISOR, decides pass or fail.

### Configuration

ADVISOR reads the process environment only, never a file. The placeholders are in `.env.example`.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ADVISOR_ENABLED` | off | Must be `1` or `true`, or the server refuses to start. `advisor install` sets it in the client config. |
| `ADVISOR_ENV` | `APP_ENV`, then `local` | `production` or `prod` always refuses to start. |
| `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT` | the working directory | The folder `run_proctor_check` may look inside. Paths outside it are refused. |
| `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY` | on | Set to `0` or `false` to allow tools that write. None exist yet. Read-only wins over `ADVISOR_GROUPS`. |
| `ADVISOR_GROUPS` | all | Comma list of tool groups to offer (`stack`, `proctor`, `booster`). See below for what each group may start. |
| `ADVISOR_PROCTOR_TIMEOUT` | `120` | Seconds before a PROCTOR run is stopped (1 to 900). |
| `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_TIMEOUT` | `60` | Seconds before a Booster plan is stopped (1 to 900). A plan is local and fast, so the default is shorter than a PROCTOR run. |
| `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN` | none | Where `upgrade_path` finds Booster when the app has no `vendor/bin/booster` of its own: the path to booster's `bin/booster` (or a `booster.phar`). The app's own `vendor/bin/booster` always wins. |
| `ADVISOR_MAX_CHARS` | `20000` | Largest piece of text one doc call returns (1000 to 45000). |
| `ADVISOR_AUDIT_LOG` | off | A file for a one-line-per-call audit log: time, tool, a hash of the arguments, outcome, duration. Arguments are hashed, never written. |
| `ADVISOR_LOG_LEVEL` | `warning` | Log level on stderr (`debug` to `emergency`). |
| `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR` | none | Folder holding the sibling stack repos; used only by `content:generate`. |
| `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` | none | A file (kept outside the repo) with private strings to strip from the bundle; used by `content:generate` and the public-posture test. See "Releasing". |
| `ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE` | none | An extra module manifest (see "Modules"). |

A bad value stops the server with a message on stderr. It does not guess.

### Commands

```
php vendor/bin/advisor mcp                          # serve over stdio (your client starts this)
php vendor/bin/advisor install [--client=claude] [--write] [--force] [--path=.]
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify               # check the bundled content against its manifest
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate [--sources=<dir>] [--check]
php vendor/bin/advisor stack-parts [--write=<readme>] [--check=<readme>]
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor [--json]              # check the install when the server does not show up
```

Stdout carries only protocol messages. Logs, warnings and stray output go to stderr, so a client never sees garbage.

### When it doesn't show up

You added the config, opened the project, and the `advisor` server is not in the list. Run:

```
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

It checks the four things that keep a server from appearing, in plain words, and changes nothing:

- **php**: the PHP on your machine satisfies ADVISOR's own `composer.json` (8.3 or newer).
- **content**: the bundled `data/` still matches its manifest.
- **client:claude**, **client:warriorgpt**, **client:cursor**, **client:vscode**: each client's MCP config: is the file there, does it have the `advisor` entry, and is the script it points at in the project? A missing file is a warning, not a failure; you only need the one client you use.
- **mcp**: the server actually starts. Doctor boots it in-process and asks for its tools.

A `fail` is something to fix; a `warn` is something you may not care about. The exit code is `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did; `--json` prints the findings as JSON.

The advisor will see you now.

### Served content

The handbook, policy, project docs, the WayneUI markup contract and WayneUI's 1.x to 2.x migration guide in `data/`
are generated from the sibling stack repositories by `content:generate` and verified at start-up against
`data/manifest.json` (a SHA-256 for every file). If a file does not match, the server refuses to start rather than
serve it. Files are cleaned on the way in: line endings are normalized and invisible characters (the TAG block,
zero-width and bidirectional controls) are stripped. Each project entry also carries its version when the project
publishes one (composer.json, else package.json, else the newest CHANGELOG heading).

Image boilerplate is trimmed from the project docs, on the way in and again when `read_project_docs` serves them: centred hero, badge and cast blocks, lone images whose target is relative or a GIF (linked or not), and rows of nothing but badges. Prose, tables and code blocks are left alone, and the bundled file itself is never rewritten at read time, so its manifest hash still holds.

Beside the generated docs, hand-written guides are kept by hand in `generator/guides/` (one Markdown file per slug),
the same way the ownership table is kept. Each is bundled into `data/guides/` and served as `advisor://guide/`;
the first is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel".

To refresh it, with the stack repos checked out side by side:

```
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack --check   # exits 1 on drift
```

CI cannot see the sibling repositories, so `composer ci` runs `content:verify`, which needs none of them.

### Releasing

ADVISOR is a public repository, so the bundle must not carry internal names. The public-posture test always checks
generic shapes (ADR numbers, open-question numbers, design-doc paths, the coordination repo). Private strings
(hostnames, people) are loaded from the file named by `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` and checked only when the file is
present.

To release:

1. Set `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one literal or `regex:` pattern per line,
   `#` comments).
2. In GitLab CI, the file comes from a masked file-type CI variable.
3. Regenerate the bundle with the file present: `php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack`.
4. Run `composer ci` to confirm the public-posture test passes.

The file is never committed. The bundle is regenerated with the file present before every release.

### Modules

Each stack project can later ship its own ADVISOR tools. Modules load only from a manifest (`modules.json`), only from
the `Waynestate\` namespace, and only if they implement the `Module` interface. Nothing scans a folder.

### Running the checks

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

```
composer ci
```

That runs `composer validate --strict`, `content:verify`, `stack-parts --check=README.md`, PHPUnit, Pint, the
agent-ready check (`site/index.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`), PHPStan (level 8, Pinstripe's raw preset, included
from `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe`), `composer audit` and the docs site check (`site/docs/` is current and every link
resolves). No PHP on your machine? Use Docker:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

Tests drive the real SDK server in-process with a small MCP client, snapshot `tools/list`, and start
`bin/advisor mcp` as a subprocess to prove stdout stays clean. To accept an intended change to the tool list, run
`ADVISOR_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 vendor/bin/phpunit`, then review and commit the diff.

### Proof run

The proof run is dev tooling, not part of the served product. It walks a corpus of app folders through the real
`bin/advisor mcp` server over stdio and writes one JSONL line per app, whose outcome is `pass`, `flagged`,
`tool-error` or `not-applicable`. Each unit is copied into a scratch folder before the server sees it; `.env`,
`auth.json` and `.git` are left behind (`.env.example` comes along), and the copy is removed when the unit is judged.
The log holds no paths and no unit directory names.

```
php bin/proof.php --units=FILE --corpus=DIR --work=DIR --out=FILE --proctor-bin=FILE --booster-bin=FILE
```

### Accessibility check

The `a11y` job in GitLab CI is Preflight's `a11y` component: axe-core 4.14.0 over `site/index.html` and
`site/docs/**/*.html`, WCAG tags only, in light and dark color schemes at 320 and 1280 px widths, plus the
reflow check for WCAG 1.4.10.

ADVISOR's own checker, `scripts/a11y/check.mjs`, runs too, as the `a11y-extra` job. It loads the same pages in light and dark themes at phone (390 px) and desktop (1440 px) width, plus one reduced-motion pass, and also requires one ``, a `lang` attribute, a non-empty title, and no horizontal scroll at phone width. Run it from the repo root (works in PowerShell):

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -e npm_config_cache=/npm-cache -v stack-npm-cache:/npm-cache -w /app/scripts/a11y mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.65.0-noble sh -c "npm install --no-audit --no-fund && node check.mjs"
```

It also runs as the `a11y-extra` job in GitLab CI.

### Safety, in short

- Off unless enabled; refuses production; refuses to start on a bad setting or a content file that fails its hash.
- Read-only by default; no tool takes a command, a URL or a free path.
- Every result is cleaned of invisible characters and labeled as data; secrets in PROCTOR output are redacted.
- `run_proctor_check` runs one fixed program with an argument array and an allowlisted environment, never a shell.
- `upgrade_path` runs Booster's read-only `plan` the same way: one fixed program, an argument array, an allowlisted command, never a shell. It plans; it never runs a hop.
- No network calls, and no model calls, from ADVISOR itself.
- The threat model, each threat mapped to the rules that answer it, is in BEST_PRACTICES.md, "Threat model".

See `BEST_PRACTICES.md`, and `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` for what is decided, assumed and not yet built.

### Why "ADVISOR"

Because registration is open, the advisor will see you now, and unlike the real one it knows which PHP version you are
allowed to be on. A little Creed energy too: it will tell you who you are, in `composer.json`, whether you like it or not.

The Wayne State app stack, surveyed

## ADVISOR

ADVISOR stands for Answers, Directions, Versions, Integrations, Standards, Onboarding and Resources.

What applies, and what's next.

An MCP server for the stack, a bit like Laravel Boost but for Wayne State. Your coding agent connects to it and gets nine read-only tools: CREED's rules and support dates, each project's docs, PROCTOR and Booster's upgrade plan. Ask it “which PHP can I build on?” and it answers from CREED's policy file, with the date and the source, instead of from whatever the model remembers.

`$ composer require --dev waynestate/advisor`

PHP 8.3 or newer. ADVISOR is on Packagist: `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.3`.

**Works alongside [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/).** You can add ADVISOR to a WELD app or to any other Wayne State PHP app.

[Ask the map](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/#ask) [Get directions](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/#directions)

The ADVISOR mark: a speech bubble holding a gold compass needle.

The magic trick, minus the magic

### Ask the map

Type a question you'd ask your coding agent. The map draws the route ADVISOR takes to answer it: which tools it calls, and which project the answer comes from.

An illustration of how your agent uses ADVISOR's tools. This page calls nothing; the real server runs on your machine, beside your app.

Control descriptions

#### Route card

“Which PHP can I build on?”

1. **Start:** your app, where your coding agent is working
2. **ADVISOR** takes the question
3. Tool `policy_lookup` with `component: php`
4. **Finish:** CREED, `policy.json`

Answer, as reference data

PHP 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support, 8.2 and 8.3 get security fixes only, and 8.1 is past its end of life.

Source: CREED `policy.json`, worked out for today.

Climb: 0 m. Everything on this route is read-only.

Read this before you set off

### Legend

ADVISOR has nine tools. These six are the ones you'll use most; the others are `owner_of`, `playbook_lookup` and `upgrade_path`. Every tool is read-only, and every answer names its source.

#### Tools

- **`list_projects`**: The stack's projects, WayneUI first, each marked built or proposed.
- **`get_project_status`**: One project: its state, package, PHP constraint, its floor under today's policy, and its next step.
- **`read_project_docs`**: A project's README or best practices, paged. For WayneUI, its markup contract too.
- **`policy_lookup`**: Whether a PHP, Laravel, Node, MySQL, Vue or Inertia version is supported today, from CREED. For Composer, the minimum version.
- **`list_stack_rules`**: CREED handbook rules with their file and line, filtered by your app's shape and by chapter.
- **`run_proctor_check`**: Runs your app's own `vendor/bin/proctor check` against the bundled policy and returns the findings.

#### Prompts

- `orient_me` a first walk round the stack, ending in three next steps
- `plan_upgrade` plans the next upgrade hop from the policy, PROCTOR and Booster's plan

#### Resources

- `advisor://policy` CREED's policy file
- `advisor://creed/<chapter>` one per handbook chapter
- `advisor://guide/<slug>` hand-written guides; first: Connect to Oracle on Citadel

#### Map symbols

- your app
- a tool call
- where the answer lives

**Run it next to Laravel Boost.** Boost knows Laravel and ADVISOR knows Wayne State, so they don't overlap. In a Laravel app the same server also runs as `php artisan mcp:start advisor`.

Turn-by-turn

### Directions

Three steps, and they're the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, because ADVISOR is one PHP command rather than a shell script.

1. ### Add it to your app
   Add it as a dev dependency. It won't start in production anyway.
   ```
   composer require --dev waynestate/advisor
   ```
2. ### Print the client config, and read it
   This writes nothing yet. Use your client's name: `claude`, `warriorgpt`, `cursor` or `vscode`. For `codex` it prints TOML to paste into `~/.codex/config.toml`.
   ```
   php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude
   ```
   ```
   {"mcpServers":{"advisor":{"command":"php","args":["vendor/bin/advisor","mcp"],"env":{"ADVISOR_ENABLED":"1"}}}}
   ```
3. ### Write it, then approve it by name
   Then open the project in your client and approve the `advisor` server when it asks. Don't commit the file it writes. It starts a program for anyone who opens the project, so `install` warns you if it isn't in `.gitignore`.
   ```
   php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
   ```

Where `install --write` puts it

- claude`.mcp.json`
- cursor`.cursor/mcp.json`
- vscode`.vscode/mcp.json`
- codex`printed only (TOML)`
- warriorgpt`.mcp.json`

Every one starts the same fixed command, `php vendor/bin/advisor mcp`. Run your client from the folder that holds `vendor/`, or set `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT`.

#### Other commands

```
# serve over stdio (your client starts this)
php vendor/bin/advisor mcp

# check the bundled content against its manifest
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify

# when the server doesn't show up in your client
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor

# every check, in the advisor repo itself
composer ci
```

#### Laravel apps

The Laravel adapter runs on `laravel/mcp` and is auto-discovered. If you want the settings in your app, publish the config:

```
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=advisor-config
```

Read out at the start line

### Briefings for your agent

Your coding agent can set ADVISOR up for you. Copy a briefing, or open it directly in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each one lists the steps and the limits, and tells the agent to ask you before it guesses.

#### Get started with ADVISOR

The agent installs ADVISOR, shows you the client config before writing it, and asks its first question once it's connected.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer connect ADVISOR to the app in this folder. ADVISOR is the MCP server of WELD, the Wayne State application stack: read-only tools that answer from CREED's policy and the stack's own docs, with the date and the source, instead of from memory.

Read first:
- https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of ADVISOR's pages, each one as Markdown. Work from them, not from memory.
- This app's composer.json and its .gitignore.
- Which coding agent you are. ADVISOR writes the config for claude, warriorgpt, cursor and vscode, and prints TOML for codex. For any other client (OpenCode, for one), print the claude config, translate it by hand, and show me before you write it.

Task:
1. Add ADVISOR as a dev dependency with `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor` (PHP 8.3 or newer).
2. Print the client config and show it to me: `php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude`, with your client's name in place of claude. Write nothing yet.
3. When I say yes, run it again with --write, and check that the file it wrote is in .gitignore.
4. If the server does not show up, run `php vendor/bin/advisor doctor` and tell me what it found.
5. Once it is connected, call list_projects, then policy_lookup for PHP, and tell me which PHP this app can build on today, with the date and the source.

Constraints:
- ADVISOR is a dev dependency and refuses to run in production. Never move it into require, and never set ADVISOR_ENV to production.
- Never commit a generated client config: it starts a program on whoever opens the project.
- The command it registers is always php vendor/bin/advisor mcp. Do not change it.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you pass --force.

Output: the config you propose, the commands you ran, the doctor result if you ran it, then your questions.
```

#### Or take the Laravel route

#### ADVISOR in a Laravel app, beside Boost

Uses the laravel/mcp adapter and adds ADVISOR to your client next to Boost, without touching Boost's entry.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding ADVISOR to a Laravel app at Wayne State University, beside Laravel Boost. ADVISOR is the MCP server of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. Boost knows Laravel; ADVISOR knows WSU. Run both.

Read first:
- https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README it links: Install, Quick start, Laravel apps and Configuration.
- composer.json, composer.lock, config/, .gitignore, .env.example, and any MCP client config already in the project (Boost writes one).

Task:
1. Add ADVISOR with `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor`. Its service provider is auto-discovered, and its Laravel adapter runs on laravel/mcp.
2. If I want the settings in the app, publish them with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=advisor-config`. They land in config/advisor.php and read the same ADVISOR_* variables.
3. Choose with me how the client starts it: `php vendor/bin/advisor install` for my client, or the Laravel way, `php artisan mcp:start advisor`. Either way it needs ADVISOR_ENABLED=1 in its environment.
4. Add it beside Boost's entry without touching Boost's. Then ask ADVISOR policy_lookup for PHP and Laravel, and list_stack_rules with the permutation that fits this app (laravel-blade, laravel-blade-vue or laravel-inertia-vue).

Constraints:
- Keep Boost. ADVISOR does not replace it.
- Off unless ADVISOR_ENABLED is set, and never in production: keep it in require-dev.
- Never commit a generated client config, and never pass --force over an entry you did not write.
- Give separate commands for Windows (PowerShell), macOS and Linux wherever they differ.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you change anything Boost owns.

Output: the client config with both servers in it, the commands you ran, the rules list_stack_rules returned, then your questions.
```

Your agent can read this page too. [llms.txt](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists the pages, [llms-full.txt](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) has all of them in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). The buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked. This page sends nothing back to us.

Hatched on the map, for a reason

### Out of bounds

An advisor can tell you what's required. It cannot sit the exam for you, and this one cannot touch your files.

- **Off unless you turn it on.** No `ADVISOR_ENABLED`, no server. `production` always refuses.
- **Read-only.** No tool takes a command, a URL or a free path, and none of them writes a file.
- **No network, no model calls.** It serves a bundled copy of the stack's docs, so it works offline.
- **Verified content.** At start-up, every bundled file is checked against a SHA-256 manifest. If one doesn't match, the server won't start.
- **Answers are data.** Every result is labeled as reference text and cleaned of invisible characters. Pass or fail is PROCTOR's call in CI.
- **Two fixed programs.** `run_proctor_check` starts only your app's own PROCTOR, with an allowlisted environment. `upgrade_path` starts only Booster's read-only `plan`, never `run`. Both get an argument array and a timeout, and neither goes through a shell.

Adjoining sheets

### The neighborhood

ADVISOR answers from a bundled copy of what these projects publish. Here is who lives where.

- [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)the interface, project 0
- [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/)the standards and policy
- [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/)checks an app
- [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)shared CI
- [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/)the coding standard
- [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/)sign-in
- [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)the runtime baseline
- [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)starts an app in any of the five shapes
- [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/)the Laravel starter app
- ADVISORyou are here
- [Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/)upgrades, one hop at a time
- [Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/)the fleet census
- [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/)the sign-in gateway
- [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)the deploy kit
- [Parity](https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/)Citadel on your computer

Here be roadmaps

### Not yet surveyed

The edges of the map. None of these is built yet, so none of them gets a command here.

- Coming soon
  ### Ask ADVISOR on the web
  A chat page. First we need to pick a model and decide what data it may see, and it will need its own accessibility review.
- Coming soon
  ### Tools that write
  Things like starting an app with Sourdough or applying a Booster hop. When they come, they stay off until you set `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY=0`.
- Coming soon
  ### Modules from each project
  The loader is built and tested. It only loads what `modules.json` lists, and no project ships a module yet.
- Coming soon
  ### HTTP transport
  stdio first. Remote needs a threat model before it needs a port.

## Changelog [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changelog)

All notable changes are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog; versions follow Semantic Versioning.

### \[Unreleased\] [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

#### Changed [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed)

- Changed: the docs, agent-ready and deploy kits are Squire 0.10.6 (docs and agent-ready tools were the 0.9.0 bytes, deploy was 0.10.2): the docs builder and agent-ready generator see every file on Docker Desktop mounts, and `oracle-check.php` loses its D-046 reference.

### \[0.3.0\] - 2026-11-09 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-3-0-2026-11-09)

#### Added [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added)

- Added: Parity is in the parts list (`generator/projects.seed.json`), after Squire: Citadel on your own computer (Citadel's PHP image, its proxy and MySQL 5.6) for any app, with or without Squire, as one Go command line for every OS on Docker or Podman (Podman recommended). `list_projects`, `get_project_status` and `read_project_docs` know it, and the stack-parts table in the README and the "Where it sits" page has fifteen rows.
- Added: `owner_of` answers "local development" (and Parity, run Citadel locally, the parity kit, Podman) with Parity: the stack's local-development answer, which replaces Squire's parity group. The deploy-files row says Squire's old parity group is deprecated, and names Parity as the one that runs `build.sh`, `deployments/` and the health check the way Citadel does.
- Added: the front page puts Parity on the map (the Reflecting Pool, top left) with a route for "Can I run my app like Citadel on my laptop?" (`get_project_status`, then `read_project_docs` for Parity) and a chip that asks it, and in the neighborhood, linked to its repository on git.wayne.edu until its site is live. The neighborhood is five across, three on a tablet and two on a phone with the odd one centered. The README cast and the readme-art kit gain Parity's mark (copied from Parity's own brand files, resized only).

#### Changed [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-1)

- Changed: the generator counts a Go module (`go.mod`) as built, like a Composer or npm package, and no longer reads a `CHANGELOG.md` heading marked unreleased (`## 0.1.0 (unreleased)`) as a published version.
- Changed: Squire's role in the parts list names what goes onto Citadel (build.sh, deployments/, the release script, the health check, the portable image) and points local runs at Parity; the front page's deploy answer does the same.
- Changed: the `wayneui-copies`, `composer-ci` and `content-drift` CI jobs and the documented Docker commands (README, MAINTAINING, Contributing, Docker, Proof) use `composer:2.11.1` pinned by its multi-arch list digest (`sha256:8de2184c...`; was `composer:2.10.3`). 2.10 is no longer maintained, and 2.11.1 fixes GHSA-c968-33g3-wh7p and GHSA-fm2w-xgf2-f9fh.
- Changed: the deploy kit is Squire 0.10.2 (was 0.10.1): the kit's Dockerfiles name every image in full (`docker.io/library/...`), the fallback base takes Composer from a `COMPOSER_IMAGE` stage, `.squire/php.ini` sets `session.cookie_samesite = Lax`, and the portable image drops `node_modules/` after the frontend build. `squire init --check` passes.
- Changed: the front page deploy layer requires CREED ^0.1.8 and HELMET ^1.3 (locked 0.1.8 and 1.3.0; were ^0.1 at 0.1.7 and ^1.0 at 1.0.1) and locks PROCTOR 0.11.1 (was 0.11.0). ADVISOR's dev tools take Pinstripe ^0.3 (locked 0.3.0, was ^0.1 at 0.1.0); before 1.0 a minor step can break, and Pint, PHPStan on Pinstripe's raw preset and the tests pass on it. The GitHub workflow pins Preflight 0.1.4's commit (`79029cc`, was an untagged commit before 0.1.4); the GitHub mirror of Preflight has no newer tag.
- Changed: CI pins the Preflight components to 0.5.0 (was 0.4.0). The composer-audit job drops its own `composer:2@sha256:b6dc...` image input, since 0.5.0's default is `composer:2.11.1` by digest, and the proctor job keeps PROCTOR's JSON report as `proctor.json` for Rollcall. The a11y component is the same at 0.5.0, so `scripts/a11y/` does not change.
- Changed: the proctor job on the front page deploy layer blocks the pipeline (no `allow_failure`). Its stale reason (unbounded constraints, CI files missing in `deploy/`) no longer holds: `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` in `deploy/` passes on PROCTOR 0.11.1 with warnings only.
- Docs: MAINTAINING's "Who maintains it" names a role, the stack maintainer, instead of a person, and says to reach them with an issue on git.wayne.edu. The CI cache comment says what the internal decision ID stood for.

### \[0.2.0\] - 2026-11-09 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-0-2026-11-09)

#### Added [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-1)

- Added: docs/threats/ explains four threats (prompt injection, path traversal, command injection, data exfiltration), where each applies, the code and tests that stop it, and what risk is left (backlog row 16).
- Added: upgrade_path takes from_php, so a project with no composer.json or no php constraint still gets a plan (Booster's --from-php); the 2026-11-08 proof run found 71 such refusals.

#### Changed [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-2)

- Changed: the deploy kit is Squire 0.10.1 (was 0.10.0): `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` copies Composer 2.11.1 (was 2.10.3, no longer maintained), and the deploy layer requires PROCTOR ^0.11 (locked 0.11.0, was ^0.8 at 0.8.0).
- Changed: the deploy kit is Squire 0.10.0 (was 0.7.1): release.sh keeps Composer and npm download caches in the app folder and the gate takes SQUIRE_PHP_RUNTIME; the compose file, health.php and .env.squire.example follow the template, and the portable image files are added.
- Changed: ADVISOR reads the policy through CREED's own reader (waynestate/creed ^0.1.8) instead of a mirrored copy, so policy_lookup and get_project_status answer exactly what PROCTOR decides; a line marked current (vue 3, inertia 2 and 3) now reads as active, where the mirror gave no state. A version the policy does not list keeps ADVISOR's answers: older than every line is end of life with a note, newer is refused with the same message.
- Docs: the README, MAINTAINING and the contributing page list everything `composer ci` runs (the agent-ready and docs site checks were missing); "What it offers" says `policy_lookup` answers end of life for a version older than the policy lists and names `upgrade_path`'s `from_php` input, as the README does; the docs overview says what main carries since 0.1.7; and the front page footer links the docs, git.wayne.edu and the GitHub mirror.
- Changed: CI pins the Preflight components to 0.4.0 (the proctor job clones the full history, so the override-approver check can read git blame).
- Changed: the deploy layer runs Squire's kit 0.7.1 (was 0.6.0): `.squire/php.ini` no longer sets the deprecated `session.sid_*` lines, web requests get a `disable_functions` list and Apache hardening (`.squire/php-web.ini`, `.squire/apache-hardening.conf`), and opcache gets production settings with `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE` as the one switch.
- Changed: the front page deploy layer requires HELMET ^1.0 (lock at 1.0.1, was 0.4.0), like the rest of the stack; its shared front controller already runs on HELMET 1.0 in Squire, Sourdough and Pinstripe.
- Changed: policy_lookup answers end of life (with a note) for a version older than every one the policy lists, instead of refusing; the 2026-11-08 proof run found 13 such refusals for PHP 5.5 to 7.3.
- Changed: CI's accessibility gate is Preflight's a11y component (light and dark, 320 and 1280 px, and the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow check); ADVISOR's own page checks (one h1, lang, title, reduced motion) stay as the a11y-extra job.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES gains a threat model: eleven threats, each mapped to the rules that answer it and to OWASP Top 10:2025, OWASP ASVS 5.0 or NIST SSDF, plus what is out of scope (ADVISOR-16).
- Changed: CI pins the Preflight components to 0.3.1 (fixed cache keys, and caches saved even when a job fails; D-072).
- Changed: CI saves its Composer and npm caches even when a job fails, so a retry after a dropped download fetches only what is missing (D-072).
- Changed: CI caches Composer and npm downloads under a fixed key, so a lock change downloads only what changed (D-072).
- Fixed: OPEN_QUESTIONS.md names the Preflight commit the GitHub workflow really pins and says the README badges are real.
- Fixed: the docs menu closes with Escape and hands focus back to its button (docs kit synced from Squire).
- Changed: the deploy layer requires PROCTOR ^0.8 (locked 0.8.0).
- Changed: the pipeline pins every Preflight CI component to 0.3.0 ([preflight@0.3.0](mailto:preflight@0.3.0)); component image inputs are plain image names, since Preflight adds the Dependency Proxy prefix itself.

### \[0.1.7\] - 2026-11-07 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-7-2026-11-07)

#### Changed [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-3)

- The front page's deploy layer (`deploy/`) completes Squire's kit 0.5.0: `oracle-check.php`, which the 0.5.0 `squire update` did not add, is written and recorded, so `squire init --check` passes. `site/assets/stack-env.js` takes the stack's one copy, with bindingless catch blocks.
- The canonical repository is git.wayne.edu (ADR-0021); docs, links and package metadata no longer point at the archived nougat copy.

#### Added [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-2)

- `owner_of` answers from an ownership table rebuilt from the stack's decisions, the one-owner-per-rule table first (version policy, lock file, `composer audit`, MySQL 5.6, `/up`, deploy files, CI contents, the parts list), then app wiring, sign-in and the coding standard. Every match carries `decision`, the decision it comes from, named by title and date. Rows gain `aliases` ("composer.lock", ".gitlab-ci.yml", "/up"), question words are ignored ("who owns composer audit" works), words match at word starts, and exact topic or alias matches come first. `content:verify` requires the decision and refuses an alias that names two rows.
- `read_project_docs` trims image boilerplate again at read time, so docs bundled before a trim rule existed are served clean without editing `data/docs`. The trim (now `Content\ImageTrim`, shared with the generator) also drops linked hero images (an image Markdown wrapped in a link) and rows of nothing but badges, which the generator used to let through (Sourdough's README hero and badge row).

New settings `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_TIMEOUT` (default 60) and `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN` (fallback when the app has no `vendor/bin/booster` of its own).

- `composer ci`: validate, content verify, PHPUnit, Pint, PHPStan level 8 (Pinstripe settings), audit. CI files for GitLab (PREFLIGHT 0.1.0) and GitHub.

## Contributing [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#contributing)

This page tells you how to make a change to ADVISOR, what rules the change must keep, and what work is still open.

### Where changes go [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#where-changes-go)

Development happens on git.wayne.edu, the canonical repository: [enterprise-apps/advisor](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/advisor) (clone `git@git.wayne.edu:enterprise-apps/advisor.git` over SSH, or `https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/advisor.git` over HTTPS). Changes, issues and merge requests go there, CI runs there on its instance runner, and tags are made there by the maintainer, with an approver. GitHub ([waynestate/advisor](https://github.com/waynestate/advisor)) is a read-only push mirror of git.wayne.edu for Packagist: nobody pushes to it.

### Build and test [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#build-and-test)

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `composer install` |
| All checks (what CI runs) | `composer ci` |
| Regenerate `data/` from the stack repos | `php bin/advisor content:generate --sources=<folder holding the stack repos>` |
| Check `data/` against the repos | add `--check` to the line above (exit 1 on drift) |
| Check `data/` against its manifest | `composer content:verify` |
| Regenerate the parts table in the README | `php bin/advisor stack-parts --write=README.md` |
| Diagnose a client setup | `php vendor/bin/advisor doctor` (in an app) |

`composer ci` runs `composer validate --strict`, `content:verify`, `stack-parts --check=README.md`, PHPUnit, Pint, the agent-ready check, PHPStan, `composer audit` and the docs site check (`composer docs:check`). CI cannot see the sibling repos, so it verifies the manifest; regenerating is a local step.

With only Docker:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

Snapshot tests are updated with `ADVISOR_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` (`$env:ADVISOR_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS = "1"` in PowerShell) before `vendor/bin/phpunit`.

### Rules a change must keep [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#rules-a-change-must-keep)

Every change to ADVISOR must keep the following practices:

1. **Read-only first.** Every tool states all four hints (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world). A tool that writes is left out unless `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY` is turned off, and that switch beats tool groups. Enforced (contract test).
2. **Narrow tools, closed schemas.** No tool takes a command, a URL or a free path. Schemas set `additionalProperties: false`, and arguments are validated again on our side. Enforced (contract test).
3. **Run other programs the safe way.** Fixed program, argument array, allowlisted environment, a timeout, and no shell. Paths are resolved and must stay inside the project root. Enforced.
4. **Keep stdout clean.** Only protocol lines go to stdout; logs, warnings and stray output go to stderr. Enforced (subprocess test).
5. **Strip invisible characters.** The TAG block, zero-width and bidirectional controls are removed from everything served and rejected in tool metadata. Enforced (contract test).
6. **Load modules from a manifest only,** from the `Waynestate\` namespace, implementing `Module`. Never scan. Enforced.
7. **Serve from verified data.** Bundled content is checked against a SHA-256 manifest at start-up and in CI; a mismatch stops the server. Enforced.
8. **Review any change to the tool list.** `tools/list` is snapshotted; a changed description is a reviewed diff. Enforced (snapshot test).
9. **Cite sources and date.** Policy answers carry the day they were worked out for and the file they came from. Enforced.

### Keeping the content fresh [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#keeping-the-content-fresh)

Run `content:generate` after any change that lands in CREED's policy or handbook, a project's README or best practices, an extra doc, or the projects seed. Commit the regenerated `data/` with the source commits in the message. To add a project to the parts list, add its `name` and `tagline` to `generator/projects.seed.json`, then regenerate and `stack-parts --write`.

Beyond a project's README and best practices, a seed may bundle further files under `extra_docs` (a map of slug to path in the project); each lands in `data/docs/<id>/<slug>.md` and in the project's docs list, and a missing file is skipped, not an error. WayneUI's entry bundles its MIGRATING.md as the `migrating` doc.

Hand-written guides live in `generator/guides/`, one Markdown file per slug, served as `advisor://guide/<slug>`. Edit them there, then run `content:generate`.

### Catch stale bundled docs [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#catch-stale-bundled-docs)

`composer content:drift` compares `data/` with a checkout of the stack repos and exits 1 when they no longer agree. It takes the folder from `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR`; without it, it prints how to run it and exits 1:

```
ADVISOR_STACK_DIR=<folder holding the stack repos> composer content:drift
```

It writes nothing. On drift it lists the files that moved; regenerate with `composer content:generate` and review the diff before committing.

Run the drift check before every tag: a release must carry docs that still match the repos it advises on.

### Releasing [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#releasing)

ADVISOR is public, so its bundle must not carry internal names. The public-posture test always checks generic shapes; private strings are loaded from a denylist file named by `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST`, kept outside the repository (in CI, a masked file-type variable).

Warning

The denylist file is never committed. The bundle is regenerated with the file present before every release.

1. Move the lines under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog) to a new `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading.
2. With the denylist file present, regenerate: `php bin/advisor content:generate --sources=<stack folder>`, then `composer ci` (the public-posture test must pass).
3. Both pipelines green for that commit. Run a secrets scan of the history.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on git.wayne.edu. Its push mirror carries the tag to GitHub, and Packagist picks it up from there.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### Open work [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#open-work)

The following items are open questions or not yet built:

- Testing on a native Windows PHP (the SDK has no Windows CI), and the MCP Inspector in CI.
- Signing of any state handed back to a client (no tool needs it yet).
- A full-capture audit mode (the threat model mapped to OWASP and NIST is done: see `BEST_PRACTICES.md` and the threat pages).
- "Ask ADVISOR" web chat: needs a model, an open stack question and an accessibility pass of its own.
- HTTP transport and OAuth: stdio first; remote needs a threat model of its own (the one in `BEST_PRACTICES.md` covers stdio only).
- Tools that write (scaffold with Sourdough, apply a Booster step): the approved list is read-only; the read-only switch and tool groups are built so they can arrive safely.
- Per-project modules in their own repositories: the loader and `Module` interface exist and are tested; the other projects have not published modules.
- WarriorGPT-backed features: no model calls until an open stack question is settled.
- Plan handles, `requestState` signing and elicitation: no tool needs state or a question to the user yet.
- Full-capture audit mode: hashes only by default; an opt-in needs a retention decision.
- MCP Inspector in CI, native Windows and macOS CI.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/contributing.html#related)

- [Upgrading](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html)
- [Releasing](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html)
- [Best practices](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html

## Refreshing the content [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#refreshing-the-content)

This page shows how to keep ADVISOR's bundled content in `data/` current with the stack: regenerate it, verify it, and check for drift.

### What is generated [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#what-is-generated)

The handbook, policy, project docs, the WayneUI markup contract and WayneUI's 1.x to 2.x migration guide in `data/` are generated from the sibling stack repositories by `content:generate` and verified at start-up against `data/manifest.json` (a SHA-256 for every file). If a file does not match, the server refuses to start rather than serve it. Files are cleaned on the way in: line endings are normalized and invisible characters (the TAG block, zero-width and bidirectional controls) are stripped. Image boilerplate is trimmed from the project docs, on the way in and again when `read_project_docs` serves them: centred hero, badge and cast blocks, lone images whose target is relative or a GIF (linked or not), and rows of nothing but badges. Prose, tables and code blocks are left alone, and the bundled file itself is never rewritten at read time, so its manifest hash still holds. Each project entry also carries its version when the project publishes one (composer.json, else package.json, else the newest CHANGELOG heading).

Beside the generated docs, hand-written guides are kept by hand in `generator/guides/` (one Markdown file per slug), the same way the ownership table is kept. Each is bundled into `data/guides/` and served as `advisor://guide/<slug>`; the first is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel".

### Regenerate [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#regenerate)

With the stack repos checked out side by side:

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack
```

`--sources` can also come from `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR`. Run `content:generate` after any change that lands in CREED's policy or handbook, a project's README or best practices, an extra doc, or the projects seed. Commit the regenerated `data/` with the source commits in the message.

The generator reads each project's folder from beside the other repos, so a stale clone gives stale docs. WayneUI's development happens on its GitLab repository and the checked-out copy is only a mirror of it: fast-forward the local wayne-ui clone to that repository's main before a resync.

To add a project to the parts list, add its `name` and `tagline` to `generator/projects.seed.json`, then regenerate and run `php bin/advisor stack-parts --write=README.md`.

Beyond a project's README and best practices, a seed may bundle further files under `extra_docs` (a map of slug to path in the project); each lands in `data/docs/<id>/<slug>.md` and in the project's docs list, and a missing file is skipped, not an error. WayneUI's entry bundles its MIGRATING.md as the `migrating` doc.

### Verify [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#verify)

CI cannot see the sibling repositories, so `composer ci` runs `content:verify`, which needs none of them:

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify
```

It checks the bundled `data/` against `data/manifest.json` (a SHA-256 for every file).

### Check for drift [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#check-for-drift)

`composer content:drift` compares `data/` with a checkout of the stack repos and exits 1 when they no longer agree. It takes the folder from `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR`; without it, it prints how to run it and exits 1:

```bash
ADVISOR_STACK_DIR=<folder holding the stack repos> composer content:drift
```

It writes nothing. On drift it lists the files that moved; regenerate with `composer content:generate` and review the diff before committing. You can also pass `--check` to `content:generate` directly:

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack --check
```

That exits 1 on drift.

The GitLab job `content-drift` does the same in CI: it clones the repos listed in `data/projects.json` with the job token, puts them in one folder, sets `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR` and runs the check. It is manual or scheduled and allowed to fail, so it cannot block main. Run the drift check before every tag: a release must carry docs that still match the repos it advises on.

### The private denylist [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#the-private-denylist)

ADVISOR is a public repository, so the bundle must not carry internal names. The public-posture test always checks generic shapes (ADR numbers, open-question numbers, design-doc paths, the coordination repo). Private strings (hostnames, people) are loaded from the file named by `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` and checked only when the file is present.

To release with the denylist:

1. Set `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one literal or `regex:` pattern per line, `#` comments).
2. In GitLab CI, the file comes from a masked file-type CI variable.
3. Regenerate the bundle with the file present: `php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack`.
4. Run `composer ci` to confirm the public-posture test passes.

Warning

The denylist file is never committed. The bundle is regenerated with the file present before every release.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html#related)

- [Releasing](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html)
- [Served content](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)

## Releasing [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html#releasing)

This page gives the numbered steps for releasing ADVISOR, from the README's "Releasing" section and MAINTAINING.md.

ADVISOR is public, so its bundle must not carry internal names. The public-posture test always checks generic shapes; private strings are loaded from a denylist file named by `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST`, kept outside the repository (in CI, a masked file-type variable). See "Releasing" in the README.

Warning

A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### Steps [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html#steps)

1. Move the lines under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog) to a new `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading.
2. With the denylist file present, regenerate: `php bin/advisor content:generate --sources=<stack folder>`, then `composer ci` (the public-posture test must pass).
3. Both pipelines green for that commit. Run a secrets scan of the history.
4. Tag `X.Y.Z` (no `v`) on git.wayne.edu. Its push mirror carries the tag to GitHub, and Packagist picks it up from there.
5. A release needs a maintainer's approval. Never move or delete a published tag.

### The denylist [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html#the-denylist)

The public-posture test always checks generic shapes (ADR numbers, open-question numbers, design-doc paths, the coordination repo). Private strings (hostnames, people) are loaded from the file named by `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` and checked only when the file is present. Set it to a file kept outside the repository (one literal or `regex:` pattern per line, `#` comments); in GitLab CI, the file comes from a masked file-type CI variable. The file is never committed. The bundle is regenerated with the file present before every release.

## One line for Claude Code [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html#one-line-for-claude-code)

This page gives the one line that connects Claude Code to ADVISOR, and the `install` command that does the same thing.

### The one line [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html#the-one-line)

If you would rather type it than generate it, this does the same as `install --client=claude --write`; project scope keeps it out of your other projects, and the same "do not commit it" warning applies:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope project advisor -e ADVISOR_ENABLED=1 -- php vendor/bin/advisor mcp
```

### The install command [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html#the-install-command)

The `install` command does the same thing and supports Claude among its clients:

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor install [--client=claude] [--write] [--force] [--path=.]
```

`install` puts `ADVISOR_ENABLED` in the client config's env block and warns when the file is not in `.gitignore`.

### Keep it out of git [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html#keep-it-out-of-git)

Warning

Approve it by name, and review the config like code. `.mcp.json` starts a program on whoever opens the project. Keep it out of git (this repo ignores it); `advisor install` warns when you have not.

## No PHP? Use Docker [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html#no-php-use-docker)

This page shows how to point your MCP client at Docker to run ADVISOR when PHP is not on your PATH.

### Point the client at Docker [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html#point-the-client-at-docker)

If PHP is not on your PATH, point the client at Docker instead. Run it from the project root, the folder that holds `vendor/`, with a hand-written `.mcp.json` like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "advisor": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "-i",
        "--rm",
        "--network",
        "none",
        "-v",
        ".:/app:ro",
        "-w",
        "/app",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_ENABLED=1",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT=/app",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack",
        "-e",
        "ADVISOR_READ_ONLY=1",
        "composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0",
        "php",
        "vendor/bin/advisor",
        "mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### What the config does [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html#what-the-config-does)

The container has no network, and the project is mounted read-only. `ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack` keeps the tools that start programs (proctor, upgrade_path) off, because those need the app's own PHP. Some clients want an absolute path in place of `.` for the mount; give them one. Advice comes in; nothing goes out.

### Where to run it [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html#where-to-run-it)

Run the client from the folder that holds `vendor/`. If it starts somewhere else, set `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT`.

### Keep it out of git [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html#keep-it-out-of-git)

This file is written by hand, so keep it out of git like the generated one. `install` never replaces a different existing `advisor` entry unless you pass `--force`, keeps your other servers, and warns when the file is not in `.gitignore`.

Warning

A client config starts a program on whoever opens the project, so do not commit a generated one; this repository ignores `.mcp.json` for that reason.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html#related)

- [One line for Claude Code](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html)
- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [Install](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

## When it does not show up [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html#when-it-does-not-show-up)

This page is the one to follow when you added the config, opened the project, and the `advisor` server is not in the list.

### Run the doctor [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html#run-the-doctor)

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor [--json]   # check the install when the server does not show up
```

It checks the four things that keep a server from appearing, in plain words, and changes nothing. `--json` prints the findings as JSON.

### What it checks [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html#what-it-checks)

- **php**: the PHP on your machine satisfies ADVISOR's own `composer.json` (8.3 or newer).
- **content**: the bundled `data/` still matches its manifest.
- **client:claude**, **client:warriorgpt**, **client:cursor**, **client:vscode**: each client's MCP config: is the file there, does it have the `advisor` entry, and is the script it points at in the project? A missing file is a warning, not a failure; you only need the one client you use.
- **mcp**: the server actually starts. Doctor boots it in-process and asks for its tools.

### Reading the result [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html#reading-the-result)

A `fail` is something to fix; a `warn` is something you may not care about. The exit code is `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did. If doctor itself cannot run, it reports a `doctor` failure and exits `2`.

The advisor will see you now.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [One line for Claude Code](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html)
- [No PHP? Use Docker](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html)
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Install](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)

## Laravel apps [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#laravel-apps)

This page shows how ADVISOR runs inside a Laravel app, beside Laravel Boost.

### The Laravel adapter [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#the-laravel-adapter)

ADVISOR ships a Laravel adapter on `laravel/mcp`, auto-discovered by the service provider. With it, the same server runs as `php artisan mcp:start advisor`, beside Boost.

Tip

Boost knows the framework, ADVISOR knows WSU. They do not overlap, so run both.

### Publish the config [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#publish-the-config)

Publish the config if you want it in the app:

```
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=advisor-config
```

### Settings [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#settings)

Settings come from the same `ADVISOR_*` variables, read through `config/advisor.php`.

Warning

The same rules apply: off unless `ADVISOR_ENABLED` is set, and never in production.

### Registering the server [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#registering-the-server)

`advisor install` always writes the plain PHP command, `php vendor/bin/advisor mcp`. The artisan route, `php artisan mcp:start advisor`, is available through the service provider.

## Modules [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/modules.html#modules)

This page explains how ADVISOR modules extend what it can answer and the rules that decide which modules load.

### How modules load [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/modules.html#how-modules-load)

Each stack project can later ship its own ADVISOR tools.

Note

Modules load only from a manifest (`modules.json`), only from the `Waynestate\` namespace, and only if they implement the `Module` interface. Nothing scans a folder.

### The manifest [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/modules.html#the-manifest)

The repository's own manifest is `modules.json` at the root:

```json
{
    "modules": [
        "Waynestate\\Advisor\\Module\\CoreModule"
    ]
}
```

It lists one module, `Waynestate\Advisor\Module\CoreModule`.

### An extra manifest [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/modules.html#an-extra-manifest)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE` | none | An extra module manifest. |

Set `ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE` to point at an extra module manifest; its default is none. An extra manifest is held to the same rules: manifest only, the `Waynestate\` namespace, and the `Module` interface.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/modules.html#related)

## Quick start [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This page takes you from a fresh install to the `advisor` server registered in your client.

1. Print the config your MCP client needs, and read it:
   ```bash
   php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude
   ```
   Expected: it prints the config your MCP client needs.
2. Write it into the project when you are happy with it:
   ```bash
   php vendor/bin/advisor install --client=claude --write
   ```
   Expected: it writes the config into the project.
3. Open the project in your client and approve the `advisor` server by name when it asks.

The command it registers is always the same fixed string, `php vendor/bin/advisor mcp`, with `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in its environment. Clients: `claude` (`.mcp.json`), `warriorgpt` (`.mcp.json`), `cursor` (`.cursor/mcp.json`), `vscode` (`.vscode/mcp.json`) and `codex` (TOML, printed only; paste it into `~/.codex/config.toml`).

### What you built [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

The `advisor` server is registered in your client, running `php vendor/bin/advisor mcp` with `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in its environment, and it is ready to answer questions about the stack.

### Next steps [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html): the environment variables.
- [One line for Claude Code](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/claude-code.html): if you would rather type it than generate it.

## Safety [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html#safety)

This page collects the safety rules ADVISOR enforces and the settings behind them, so you know what it will and will not do.

Each control is also written up as a threat page: [prompt injection](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html), [path traversal](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html), [command injection](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html) and [data exfiltration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html).

### Safety, in short [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html#safety-in-short)

- Off unless enabled; refuses production; refuses to start on a bad setting or a content file that fails its hash.
- Read-only by default; no tool takes a command, a URL or a free path.
- Every result is cleaned of invisible characters and labeled as data; secrets in PROCTOR output are redacted.
- `run_proctor_check` runs one fixed program with an argument array and an allowlisted environment, never a shell.
- `upgrade_path` runs Booster's read-only `plan` the same way: one fixed program, an argument array, an allowlisted command, never a shell. It plans; it never runs a hop.
- No network calls, and no model calls, from ADVISOR itself.

### Settings that enforce it [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html#settings-that-enforce-it)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY` | on | Set to `0` or `false` to allow tools that write. None exist yet. Read-only wins over `ADVISOR_GROUPS`. |
| `ADVISOR_ENV` | `APP_ENV`, then `local` | `production` or `prod` always refuses to start. |
| `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT` | the working directory | The folder `run_proctor_check` may look inside. Paths outside it are refused. |
| `ADVISOR_AUDIT_LOG` | off | A file for a one-line-per-call audit log: time, tool, a hash of the arguments, outcome, duration. Arguments are hashed, never written. |
| `ADVISOR_GROUPS` | all | Comma list of tool groups to offer (`stack`, `proctor`, `booster`). The [What it offers](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html) page says what each group may start. |

Warning

A bad value stops the server with a message on stderr. It does not guess.

### Best practices [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html#best-practices)

From `BEST_PRACTICES.md`, the safety rules:

- **Run it in development only.** It refuses to start unless `ADVISOR_ENABLED` is set and refuses in production. Enforced.
- **Keep secrets out of what you ask.** Do not paste tokens into prompts. Audit logs hold hashes, never arguments, and PROCTOR output is redacted. Enforced.
- **Read-only first.** Every tool states all four hints (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world). A tool that writes is left out unless `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY` is turned off, and that switch beats tool groups. Enforced (contract test).
- **Narrow tools, closed schemas.** No tool takes a command, a URL or a free path. Schemas set `additionalProperties: false`, and arguments are validated again on our side. Enforced (contract test).
- **Run other programs the safe way.** Fixed program, argument array, allowlisted environment, a timeout, and no shell. Paths are resolved and must stay inside the project root. Enforced.
- **Strip invisible characters.** The TAG block, zero-width and bidirectional controls are removed from everything served and rejected in tool metadata. Enforced (contract test).
- **Serve from verified data.** Bundled content is checked against a SHA-256 manifest at start-up and in CI; a mismatch stops the server. Enforced.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html#related)

- [What it offers](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html)
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Best practices](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)
- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [Install](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)
