Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html

## Served content [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#served-content)

This page explains what content ADVISOR serves, where it comes from, and how to keep it fresh.

### What is served [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#what-is-served)

The handbook, policy, project docs, the WayneUI markup contract and WayneUI's 1.x to 2.x migration guide in `data/` are generated from the sibling stack repositories. `data/` is generated, never hand-edited: `policy.json` and `handbook/` from CREED, `projects.json` from each project repo and `generator/projects.seed.json` (state, package, version, PHP floor), plus each project's README, best practices and any extra docs its seed names.

Each project entry also carries its version when the project publishes one (composer.json, else package.json, else the newest CHANGELOG heading).

Beyond a project's README and best practices, a seed may bundle further files under `extra_docs` (a map of slug to path in the project); each lands in `data/docs/<id>/<slug>.md` and in the project's docs list, and a missing file is skipped, not an error. WayneUI's entry bundles its MIGRATING.md as the `migrating` doc.

### Verified at start-up [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#verified-at-start-up)

Content is generated by `content:generate` and verified at start-up against `data/manifest.json` (a SHA-256 for every file).

Warning

If a file does not match, the server refuses to start rather than serve it.

Files are cleaned on the way in: line endings are normalized and invisible characters (the TAG block, zero-width and bidirectional controls) are stripped. Image boilerplate is trimmed from the project docs, on the way in and again when `read_project_docs` serves them: centred hero, badge and cast blocks, lone images whose target is relative or a GIF (linked or not), and rows of nothing but badges. Prose, tables and code blocks are left alone, and the bundled file itself is never rewritten at read time, so its manifest hash still holds.

### Hand-written guides [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#hand-written-guides)

Beside the generated docs, hand-written guides are kept by hand in `generator/guides/` (one Markdown file per slug), the same way the ownership table is kept. Each is bundled into `data/guides/` and served as `advisor://guide/<slug>`; the first is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel". Edit them there, then run `content:generate`.

### Refreshing the content [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#refreshing-the-content)

To refresh it, with the stack repos checked out side by side:

```
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate --sources=/path/to/stack --check   # exits 1 on drift
```

Run `content:generate` after any change that lands in CREED's policy or handbook, a project's README or best practices, an extra doc, or the projects seed. Commit the regenerated `data/` with the source commits in the message.

The generator reads each project's folder from beside the other repos, so a stale clone gives stale docs. WayneUI's development happens on its GitLab repository and the checked-out copy is only a mirror of it: fast-forward the local wayne-ui clone to that repository's main before a resync.

CI cannot see the sibling repositories, so `composer ci` runs `content:verify`, which needs none of them.

### Catching drift [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#catching-drift)

`composer content:drift` compares `data/` with a checkout of the stack repos and exits 1 when they no longer agree. It takes the folder from `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR`; without it, it prints how to run it and exits 1. It writes nothing. On drift it lists the files that moved; regenerate with `composer content:generate` and review the diff before committing.

The GitLab job `content-drift` does the same in CI: it clones the repos listed in `data/projects.json` with the job token, puts them in one folder, sets `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR` and runs the check. It is manual or scheduled and allowed to fail, so it cannot block main. Run the drift check before every tag: a release must carry docs that still match the repos it advises on.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/served-content.html#related)

- [What it offers](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)
- [Releasing](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html)

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html

## What it offers [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html#what-it-offers)

ADVISOR gives a coding agent nine read-only tools, plus two prompts and three resource routes, and each answer says where it came from.

### Tools [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html#tools)

Nine tools, all read-only. Each one says where its answer came from:

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_projects` | The stack's projects, WayneUI first, with built or proposed state, package and version. |
| `get_project_status` | One project: state, package, version, PHP constraint, its floor under today's policy, next step. |
| `read_project_docs` | A project's README, best practices, or (WayneUI only) markup contract and 1.x to 2.x migration guide, paged. |
| `policy_lookup` | Support state for a runtime or tool (and an optional version) from CREED, as of today, worked out by CREED's own reader (`waynestate/creed`), the one PROCTOR carries a copy of. A version older than every one the policy lists is answered as end of life, with a note. |
| `list_stack_rules` | CREED handbook rules, each with its file and line, filtered by app permutation and chapter. |
| `owner_of` | Answers "which project owns X?" from the bundled ownership table, built from the stack's one-owner-per-rule decision first: the owner, its role, the projects around it, and the decision each answer comes from. Pass a topic or the whole question ("who owns composer audit"). |
| `playbook_lookup` | A shared value by key, or every key: an environment variable of the same name wins, then Playbook; secret-looking keys are refused. |
| `run_proctor_check` | Runs the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor check` against the bundled policy and returns the findings. |
| `upgrade_path` | Plans the app's PHP and/or Laravel upgrade, one supported hop at a time, via Booster's read-only `plan`. Inputs: from_php (the version the app runs today, when the project names none), to_php, to_laravel. |

Note

Everything ADVISOR returns is labeled as reference data. PROCTOR in CI, not ADVISOR, decides pass or fail.

### Groups [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html#groups)

The groups split by what they may start: `stack` never starts a program, `proctor` starts the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor`, and `booster` starts Booster's read-only `plan` (never `run`). Set `ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack` when you want ADVISOR as pure reference material.

### Resources [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html#resources)

| Resource | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `advisor://policy` | CREED's policy file. |
| `advisor://creed/<chapter>` | One per handbook chapter. |
| `advisor://guide/<slug>` | Hand-written guides; the first is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel". |

### Prompts [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html#prompts)

Prompts: `orient_me` and `plan_upgrade`.

Here is what that looks like when you ask. Each numbered control point is one of the tools above, with the arguments the front page's own route table sends:

![A topographic field map of the stack. Three questions are plotted from 'your app' through the ADVISOR advising office to the project that answers. 'Which PHP can I build on?' goes through policy_lookup (component: php) to CREED's policy.json. 'Which security headers do I need?' goes through list_stack_rules (chapter: runtime-and-headers) and read_project_docs (project: helmet) to HELMET. 'How do I get off PHP 8.2?' goes through the plan_upgrade prompt, policy_lookup, run_proctor_check and read_project_docs (project: booster) to Booster.](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/route.svg)

## Where it sits in WELD [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/where-it-sits.html#where-it-sits-in-weld)

This page shows where ADVISOR sits among the parts of the Wayne State application stack and in WELD.

### The stack and WELD [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/where-it-sits.html#the-stack-and-weld)

The stack is the Wayne State application stack. WELD, Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed, is its Laravel starter app. You can add ADVISOR to a WELD app or to any other Wayne State PHP app, and in either case it is the part of the stack that talks to your coding agent.

### The parts [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/where-it-sits.html#the-parts)

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **WayneUI** | interface (project 0) |
| **CREED** | version policy and written standards |
| **PROCTOR** | checks an app |
| **SESAME** | sign-in inside the app |
| **HELMET** | runtime baseline |
| **Sourdough** | starter |
| **Preflight** | CI components |
| **Pinstripe** | coding standard |
| **Booster** | upgrades |
| **Rollcall** | fleet census |
| **Drawbridge** | sign-in gateway |
| **Squire** | deploy kit |
| **Parity** | Citadel on your computer |
| **ADVISOR** | MCP server |
| **WELD** | the Laravel starter app |

### What each part is [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/where-it-sits.html#what-each-part-is)

ADVISOR serves a bundled copy of what these projects publish, so it works offline. Each part:

- **WayneUI** is the interface, project 0 of the stack. ADVISOR bundles its markup contract and its 1.x to 2.x migration guide.
- **CREED** is the version policy and the written standards. ADVISOR bundles its policy file and handbook, and reads the policy through CREED's own reader (`waynestate/creed`).
- **PROCTOR** checks an app.
- **SESAME** handles sign-in inside the app.
- **HELMET** is the runtime baseline.
- **Sourdough** is the starter.
- **Preflight** provides the CI components (php-test, composer-audit, proctor and a11y).
- **Pinstripe** is the coding standard; PHPStan includes its raw preset.
- **Booster** does the upgrades.
- **Rollcall** is the fleet census.
- **Drawbridge** is the sign-in gateway.
- **Squire** is the deploy kit; the front page's deploy layer is generated with it.
- **Parity** runs Citadel on your own computer: Citadel's PHP image, its proxy and MySQL 5.6, for any app, with or without Squire. It is a Go command line for every OS, on Docker or Podman (Podman recommended), and it replaces Squire's parity group. Its site is [parity.apps.wayne.edu](https://parity.apps.wayne.edu/), and its repository is [enterprise-apps/parity](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/parity) on git.wayne.edu.
- **ADVISOR** is the MCP server, the part of the stack that talks to your coding agent.
- **WELD** is the Laravel starter app: Wired, Everything, Linked, Deployed.

Note

ADVISOR does not replace Laravel Boost. Boost knows Laravel; ADVISOR knows WSU. Run both.

## Overview [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

**What applies, and what's next.**

This page tells you what ADVISOR is, how to run it, and where to go next.

ADVISOR is an MCP server for the Wayne State application stack, a bit like Laravel Boost but for WSU. It orients a developer who is new to the stack and gives their coding agent nine read-only tools into it: the CREED standards and policy, PROCTOR results, the upgrade path, the WayneUI markup contract and migration guide, SESAME and HELMET guidance, and the parts list. Ask it "which PHP can I build on?" and it answers from the policy file, with the date and the source, instead of from whatever the model remembers.

It is read-only. It cannot write a file, run a shell command, or call out to the network. The two things it can start are the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor` and Booster's read-only `plan`, both with a fixed argument shape.

> Every WSU student has an advisor. Now every WSU app does too, and this one answers email.

### Install and run [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#install-and-run)

Add it to the app as a dev dependency, then run it:

```bash
composer require --dev waynestate/advisor
php vendor/bin/advisor
```

The command is `php vendor/bin/advisor`. This works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, because it is one PHP command and not a shell script.

### Pick your path [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): register the `advisor` server with your client.
- [Install](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): what it needs and how to add it to an app.
- [What it offers](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html): the nine read-only tools.
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html): the environment variables.

### Status [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#status)

Current release 0.3.0. PHP ^8.3, license MIT, MCP SDK 0.9.0. New in 0.3.0: Parity, Citadel on your own computer, is the fifteenth part of the stack, so `list_projects`, `get_project_status`, `read_project_docs` and `owner_of` ("local development") know it; the bundle is resynced with the stack's 2026-11-09 night main branches; and CI runs on Composer 2.11.1 and Preflight 0.5.0. The [changelog](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html) has the full list, and [Upgrading](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html) the one step it needs. Agent-ready index: [llms.txt](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt).

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#related)

- [Install](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)
- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [What it offers](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html)

## Install [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

This page shows what ADVISOR needs and how to add it to a Wayne State PHP app.

### Requirements [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

PHP 8.3 or newer (8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 are tested). The package requires:

- PHP `^8.3`
- extensions `ext-fileinfo`, `ext-json` and `ext-mbstring`
- `composer/semver` `^3.0`
- `mcp/sdk` `0.9.0`
- `opis/json-schema` `^2.4`
- `psr/log` `^3.0`
- `symfony/console` `^7.4 || ^8.0`
- `symfony/process` `^7.4 || ^8.0`
- `waynestate/creed` `^0.1.8` (CREED's policy reader)

The platform is pinned to PHP 8.3.0 in `composer.json`.

### Install [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

Add it to the app as a dev dependency:

```bash
composer require --dev waynestate/advisor
```

The command is then `php vendor/bin/advisor`. This works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, because it is one PHP command and not a shell script.

ADVISOR is on Packagist: `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.3`. No extra repository needed.

Note

Native Windows is not yet proven. ADVISOR is one PHP command, so it is built to run the same everywhere, but it has not been proven on native Windows. If you are on Windows, [use Docker](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html).

### Verify [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Check the install with:

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

It checks the four things that keep a server from appearing, in plain words, and changes nothing:

- **php**: the PHP on your machine satisfies ADVISOR's own `composer.json` (8.3 or newer).
- **content**: the bundled `data/` still matches its manifest.
- **client:claude**, **client:warriorgpt**, **client:cursor**, **client:vscode**: each client's MCP config.
- **mcp**: the server actually starts. Doctor boots it in-process and asks for its tools.

A `fail` is something to fix; a `warn` is something you may not care about. The exit code is `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did; `--json` prints the findings as JSON.

### Next steps [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): register the `advisor` server with a client.
- [What it offers](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-it-offers.html): the nine read-only tools.
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html): the environment variables.

- [Overview](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.html)
- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)

## Best practices [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#best-practices)

These are the rules ADVISOR holds itself to, the short version for people who use ADVISOR and people who add to it, with the test that enforces each rule where there is one.

Tags: Enforced (code or CI stops the bad outcome), Documented (written down only), Not yet (a gap).

### Approve it by name, and review the config like code [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#approve-it-by-name-and-review-the-config-like-code)

`.mcp.json` starts a program on whoever opens the project. Keep it out of git (this repo ignores it); `advisor install` warns when you have not. Enforced (warning).

### Treat answers as data [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#treat-answers-as-data)

Every result says where it came from and that it is reference text. PROCTOR in CI decides pass or fail; ADVISOR never does. Enforced (labels), Documented (the rule).

### Run it in development only [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#run-it-in-development-only)

It refuses to start unless `ADVISOR_ENABLED` is set and refuses in production. Enforced.

### Keep secrets out of what you ask [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#keep-secrets-out-of-what-you-ask)

Do not paste tokens into prompts. Audit logs hold hashes, never arguments, and PROCTOR output is redacted. Enforced.

### Run Boost beside it in Laravel apps [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#run-boost-beside-it-in-laravel-apps)

Boost knows the framework, ADVISOR knows WSU. They do not overlap. Documented.

### Read-only first [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#read-only-first)

Every tool states all four hints (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world). A tool that writes is left out unless `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY` is turned off, and that switch beats tool groups. Enforced (contract test).

### Narrow tools, closed schemas [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#narrow-tools-closed-schemas)

No tool takes a command, a URL or a free path. Schemas set `additionalProperties: false`, and arguments are validated again on our side. Enforced (contract test).

### Run other programs the safe way [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#run-other-programs-the-safe-way)

Fixed program, argument array, allowlisted environment, a timeout, and no shell. Paths are resolved and must stay inside the project root. Enforced.

### Keep stdout clean [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#keep-stdout-clean)

Only protocol lines go to stdout; logs, warnings and stray output go to stderr. Enforced (subprocess test).

### Strip invisible characters [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#strip-invisible-characters)

The TAG block, zero-width and bidirectional controls are removed from everything served and rejected in tool metadata. Enforced (contract test).

### Load modules from a manifest only [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#load-modules-from-a-manifest-only)

From the `Waynestate\` namespace, implementing `Module`. Never scan. Enforced.

### Serve from verified data [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#serve-from-verified-data)

Bundled content is checked against a SHA-256 manifest at start-up and in CI; a mismatch stops the server. Enforced.

### Review any change to the tool list [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#review-any-change-to-the-tool-list)

`tools/list` is snapshotted; a changed description is a reviewed diff. Enforced (snapshot test).

### Cite sources and date [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#cite-sources-and-date)

Policy answers carry the day they were worked out for and the file they came from. Enforced.

### Threat model [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#threat-model)

`BEST_PRACTICES.md` carries the threat model: eleven threats, each mapped to the rules above and to OWASP Top 10:2025, OWASP ASVS 5.0 or NIST SSDF, plus what is out of scope. Four of them have a page of their own: [prompt injection](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html), [path traversal](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html), [command injection](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html) and [data exfiltration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html).

### Not yet [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#not-yet)

- Testing on a native Windows PHP (the SDK has no Windows CI), and the MCP Inspector in CI.
- Signing of any state handed back to a client (no tool needs it yet).
- A full-capture audit mode.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#related)

- [Proof](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Safety](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html)
- [Changelog](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

Every command the `advisor` CLI takes, and what it does.

### Running a command [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#running-a-command)

Run any command with `php vendor/bin/advisor <command>`. This is one PHP command, not a shell script, so it works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. The `mcp` command is started by your MCP client, not by you.

```
php vendor/bin/advisor mcp                          # serve over stdio (your client starts this)
php vendor/bin/advisor install [--client=claude] [--write] [--force] [--path=.]
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify               # check the bundled content against its manifest
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate [--sources=<dir>] [--check]
php vendor/bin/advisor stack-parts [--write=<readme>] [--check=<readme>]
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor [--json]              # check the install when the server does not show up
```

Stdout carries only protocol messages. Logs, warnings and stray output go to stderr, so a client never sees garbage.

### Commands [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands-1)

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/advisor doctor` | Check the install: PHP, the bundled content, the client config, and the server. |
| `bin/advisor install` | Print (or with --write, write) the MCP client config that starts ADVISOR. |
| `bin/advisor mcp` | Serve ADVISOR to an MCP client over stdio (started by the client, not by hand). |
| `bin/advisor stack-parts` | Render the stack parts table from the seed; write or check the marked block in a README. |
| `bin/advisor content:generate` | Rebuild the bundled content from the stack repositories (--check only compares). |
| `bin/advisor content:verify` | Check the bundled content against its manifest. |

#### `bin/advisor doctor` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-doctor)

Check the install: PHP, the bundled content, the client config, and the server.

Usage: `bin/advisor doctor [--json]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print the findings as JSON. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor install` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-install)

Print (or with --write, write) the MCP client config that starts ADVISOR.

Usage: `bin/advisor install [-c|--client CLIENT] [--write] [--force] [--path PATH]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--client=VALUE` | claude, warriorgpt, cursor, vscode or codex. | `claude` |
| `--write` | Write the file in the project instead of printing it. |  |
| `--force` | Replace an existing, different "advisor" entry. |  |
| `--path=VALUE` | Project folder to write into. | `.` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor mcp` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-mcp)

Serve ADVISOR to an MCP client over stdio (started by the client, not by hand).

Usage: `bin/advisor mcp`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor stack-parts` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-stack-parts)

Render the stack parts table from the seed; write or check the marked block in a README.

Usage: `bin/advisor stack-parts [--write WRITE] [--check CHECK]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--write=VALUE` | Replace the block between the stack-parts markers in this file (repeatable) |  |
| `--check=VALUE` | Exit 1 when the block in this file is stale (repeatable) |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor content:generate` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-content-generate)

Rebuild the bundled content from the stack repositories (--check only compares).

Usage: `bin/advisor content:generate [-s|--sources SOURCES] [--check]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-s`, `--sources=VALUE` | Folder that holds the stack repositories (creed, proctor, wayne-ui, ...). Default: ADVISOR_STACK_DIR. |  |
| `--check` | Exit 1 when the bundle differs from what the sources produce; write nothing. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor content:verify` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-content-verify)

Check the bundled content against its manifest.

Usage: `bin/advisor content:verify`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### Options every command accepts [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options-every-command-accepts)

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command |  |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed |  |
| \`-v | -vv | -vvv`, `--verbose\` |
| `-V`, `--version` | Display this application version |  |
| `--ansi` | Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output |  |
| `--no-ansi` | Negate the "--ansi" option |  |
| `-n`, `--no-interaction` | Do not ask any interactive question |  |

### Exit codes [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes)

- `content:generate --check` exits `1` on drift, when the bundled content no longer matches the source repos.
- `doctor` exits `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did; `--json` prints the findings as JSON. If doctor itself cannot run, it reports a `doctor` failure and exits `2`.
- `composer content:drift` exits `1` when `data/` no longer matches the stack repos, or when `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR` is not set.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [When it does not show up](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html)
- [Refreshing the content](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/refreshing-the-content.html)
- [Configuration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html

## Configuration [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

ADVISOR reads the process environment only, never a file. This page lists every variable with its default and its meaning, and the placeholders are in `.env.example`. Nothing in ADVISOR needs a secret, key, certificate, token or host, so every setting is optional.

### Environment variables [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#environment-variables)

| Variable | Meaning | Default | Read in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ADVISOR_AUDIT_LOG | A file for a one-line-per-call audit log: time, tool, a hash of the arguments, outcome, duration. Arguments are hashed, never written. | off | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN | Where `upgrade_path` finds Booster when the app has no `vendor/bin/booster` of its own: the path to booster's `bin/booster` (or a `booster.phar`). The app's own `vendor/bin/booster` always wins. | none | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_BOOSTER_TIMEOUT | Seconds before a Booster plan is stopped (1 to 900). A plan is local and fast, so the default is shorter than a PROCTOR run. | `60` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_ENABLED | Must be `1` or `true`, or the server refuses to start. `advisor install` sets it in the client config. | off | src/Command/ClientConfig.php |
| ADVISOR_ENV | `production` or `prod` always refuses to start. | `APP_ENV`, then `local` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_GROUPS | Comma list of tool groups to offer (`stack`, `proctor`, `booster`). See below for what each group may start. | all | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_LOG_LEVEL | Log level on stderr (`debug` to `emergency`). | `warning` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_MAX_CHARS | Largest piece of text one doc call returns (1000 to 45000). | `20000` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE | An extra module manifest (see "Modules"). | none | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST | A file (kept outside the repo) with private strings to strip from the bundle; used by `content:generate` and the public-posture test. See "Releasing". | none | src/Content/Denylist.php |
| ADVISOR_PROCTOR_TIMEOUT | Seconds before a PROCTOR run is stopped (1 to 900). | `120` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT | The folder `run_proctor_check` may look inside. Paths outside it are refused. | the working directory | src/Command/DoctorCommand.php |
| ADVISOR_READ_ONLY | Set to `0` or `false` to allow tools that write. None exist yet. Read-only wins over `ADVISOR_GROUPS`. | on | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_STACK_DIR | Folder holding the sibling stack repos; used only by `content:generate`. | none | src/Command/ContentGenerateCommand.php |

### Example [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#example)

A short example, with placeholder values:

```bash
ADVISOR_ENABLED=1
ADVISOR_ENV=local
ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT=/path/to/your/app
ADVISOR_AUDIT_LOG=/path/to/advisor-audit.log
```

`advisor install` sets `ADVISOR_ENABLED` in the client config for you.

Warning

A bad value stops the server with a message on stderr. It does not guess.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#related)

- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Quick start](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [No PHP? Use Docker](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docker.html)
- [Safety](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html)

## Proof [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page walks through `composer ci`, the one command that proves the build, and what each step of it proves.

The same command runs on GitLab and GitHub.

### Last run [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer validate --strict` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: `./composer.json is valid` | 1 s |
| `content:verify` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: `data/ is sound.` | under 1 s |
| `stack-parts --check=README.md` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: the stack-parts block is up to date in 1 file | under 1 s |
| `phpunit` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: 282 tests, 1535 assertions, 1 skipped | 56 s |
| `pint --test` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: 111 files | 1 s |
| `site:agent-ready-check` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: 31 file(s) current | under 1 s |
| `phpstan analyse` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: no errors | 2 s |
| `composer audit` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: no security advisories | 1 s |
| `docs:check` | 2026-11-09 | 7818dae | pass: 26 page(s) current | under 1 s |

Commit 7818dae is the 0.2.0 release. The skipped test is the private half of `PublicPostureTest`, which runs only when `ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST` is set. To refresh this table, re-run `composer ci` (or each command above) on the commit you want to record and rewrite the date, commit, results and durations. Every check this page names was run on 2026-11-09 in Docker (`composer:2.11.1`, PHP 8.5) on a copy of the tracked files; none was skipped. The proof run (`bin/proof.php`, see the README) is dev tooling outside `composer ci` and was not run: it needs a corpus of app folders and the PROCTOR and Booster binaries.

### The command [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#the-command)

```
composer ci
```

No PHP on your machine? Use Docker:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2.11.1@sha256:8de2184c6de224f4689e8f80ed5f5edaf0030b6b8b7839a22a2bcb6722ac87d0 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

### composer validate --strict [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#composer-validate-strict)

Runs `composer validate --strict` on the package metadata.

### content:verify [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#content-verify)

Runs `php bin/advisor content:verify`, which checks the bundled content against its manifest. CI cannot see the sibling repositories, so `composer ci` runs `content:verify`, which needs none of them.

### stack-parts --check=README.md [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#stack-parts-check-readme-md)

Runs `php bin/advisor stack-parts --check=README.md`, which proves the parts table in the README still matches `generator/projects.seed.json`.

### PHPUnit [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#phpunit)

Runs `phpunit`. Tests drive the real SDK server in-process with a small MCP client, snapshot `tools/list`, and start `bin/advisor mcp` as a subprocess to prove stdout stays clean.

Tip

To accept an intended change to the tool list, run `ADVISOR_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 vendor/bin/phpunit`, then review and commit the diff.

### Pint [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#pint)

Runs `pint --test`, the style check.

### site:agent-ready-check [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#site-agent-ready-check)

Fails when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here.

### PHPStan [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#phpstan)

Runs `phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G`: level 8, Pinstripe's raw preset, included from `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe`.

### composer audit [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#composer-audit)

Runs `composer audit`.

### docs:check [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#docs-check)

Fails when `site/docs/` is stale or a docs page has a broken link, block or nav entry.

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#related)

- [Best practices](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Releasing](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/deploying/releasing.html)
- [Changelog](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html

## Command injection [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html#command-injection)

An attacker who controls a tool argument wants ADVISOR to start a program or run a command the developer never approved, using the server's privileges on the developer's machine.

### Where it applies in ADVISOR [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html#where-it-applies-in-advisor)

Only two tools start a child process, and both do it on purpose:

- `run_proctor_check` starts the app's own `vendor/bin/proctor` (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:58-63`).
- `upgrade_path` starts Booster's `plan`, preferring the app's own `vendor/bin/booster` and falling back to the operator's configured path (`src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:96-118`).

Everything the model sends for those tools flows into the argument list of one of those two commands, so the argument list is the attack surface. No other tool starts a process; the reference tools answer from bundled files only.

The server usually runs on the developer's own machine, next to the credentials it protects, which is why no-shell matters here more than in a container.

Both tools take a few extra arguments, but each is validated against a closed set before it reaches the command: the check ids against a fixed list (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:46-50`), and the version targets against strict patterns (`src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:37-45`).

### What stops it [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html#what-stops-it)

- **The program is fixed, not chosen.** The binary is located only in the project's own `vendor/bin` or the operator's configured setting; nothing a model sends picks which program runs (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:58-63`, `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:96-118`). The fallback path must look like a PHP script or phar before it is accepted (`src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:107-113`, `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:121-127`).
- **The subcommand is part of the allowlist.** PROCTOR may only run `check` and Booster only `plan`; a third slot holding anything else is refused (`src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:53`, `src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:81`).
- **Argument array, no shell.** The process runner hands Symfony Process an argv array with no stdin, so there is no shell to interpret spaces, semicolons or quotes (`src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:30-31`).
- **The whole command shape is allowlisted.** Before anything runs, `CommandAllowlist` checks the exact shape `[php, script, subcommand, --option=value ...]`: only known options, each at most once, each value matched against a regex, and the required options present (`src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:51-70` for PROCTOR, `src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:79-98` for Booster; option tables at `src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:20-26` and `src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:35-42`). Booster's `run`, the subcommand that edits files, is deliberately absent (`src/Security/CommandAllowlist.php:28-31`).
- **The run is capped.** A timeout stops a runaway child, and its output is truncated to 2 MB before it is read (`src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:17`, `src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:39-43`).

The tests prove the refusals: another program, another script, another subcommand, an extra flag, a flag in the path slot, a bare argument, a changed format, a duplicate option, a timeout of `1;rm -rf /`, a missing policy and a single-dash option are all refused for PROCTOR (`tests/Security/CommandAllowlistTest.php:35-62`); Booster's `run` subcommand and a `--from-php=7.4;rm` value are refused the same way (`tests/Security/CommandAllowlistTest.php:83-103`). The contract test adds that no tool may be named like a shell or take a free-form command, code, sql or url argument (`tests/Contract/ServerContractTest.php:59-68`).

A reviewer can check this by reading the two bad-command providers in `tests/Security/CommandAllowlistTest.php` and running `composer test`.

### What is left [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html#what-is-left)

The allowlist pins the shape of the command; it does not audit what the child program does. PROCTOR and BOOSTER run with full access to the project folder and their own logic, so a vulnerability in either one is outside this control.

The environment handed to the child is scrubbed (see [Data exfiltration](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html)), and the timeout caps how long it runs, but neither limit stops a well-behaved-looking program from reading files inside the project, which is what it was started to do.

A misconfigured machine can point `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN` at a different PHP script; the allowlist still pins what it may be told to do, but the choice of program is then the operator's. And the allowlist is enforced inside ADVISOR, on the machine that runs it: a compromised ADVISOR install could simply stop calling it.

---

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html

## Data exfiltration [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html#data-exfiltration)

An attacker wants a secret (an environment variable, a token, a key, a file's contents) to leave the machine and land somewhere the model, a log, or a report can carry it out.

### Where it applies in ADVISOR [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html#where-it-applies-in-advisor)

Three channels could carry a secret out:

- The child processes behind `run_proctor_check` and `upgrade_path` inherit the server's environment, and whatever they print becomes a tool result (`src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:21-30`).
- Finding messages and plan warnings quote the project's own files (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:116`, `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:209`).
- The optional audit log records every tool call (`src/Server/AuditLog.php:20-35`).

ADVISOR itself makes no network calls, so "out" means into the model's context or onto disk in a log; the client then decides what happens to that text (`docs/guides/safety.md:19`). A fourth, quieter channel is the tool descriptions and prompts the client reads before any call; they ship in the repo and are scanned for hidden characters (`tests/Contract/ServerContractTest.php:70-83`).

### What stops it [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html#what-stops-it)

- **Child processes get an allowlisted environment.** Only the names in `EnvAllowlist::NAMES` survive; everything else, including the app's `.env` values, tokens and cloud keys, is removed before the process starts (`src/Security/EnvAllowlist.php:18-24`, applied at `src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:30`).
- **Secret-shaped text is redacted.** Every string that came from a child process or a project file passes through the redactor, which blanks credential-shaped `key=value` pairs, Bearer tokens, PEM private-key blocks and well-known token shapes (`src/Security/Redactor.php:16-26`, `src/Security/Redactor.php:28-41`; applied at `src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:82`, `src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:116`, `src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:142` and `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:80`, `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:209`).
- **Paths in results are project-relative**, so a report does not reveal where the project lives on the host (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:127`, `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:140`), and the policy file is described rather than located (`src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:172-174`).
- **The audit log stores a hash of the arguments, never the arguments** (`src/Server/AuditLog.php:28`).
- **`playbook_lookup` refuses secret-looking keys.** A key ending in SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN or KEY is refused before any source is consulted (`src/Playbook/Settings.php:17`, `src/Playbook/Settings.php:51-55`).
- **Output is capped.** Child output beyond 2 MB is dropped before it is read, so a chatty process cannot flood the context with data (`src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:17`, `src/Security/SymfonyProcessRunner.php:39-43`).
- **The server holds no secrets of its own.** ADVISOR needs no API keys; when the optional Playbook package is present it is the only holder of shared values, and the lookup tool is the only door to it.

The tests prove the first two: `APP_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `COMPOSER_AUTH` do not survive into a child environment while `PATH` does (`tests/Security/EnvAndRedactionTest.php:13-30`), and credential shapes plus a private-key block are blanked while plain words stay (`tests/Security/EnvAndRedactionTest.php:32-52`). The contract test keeps private-key blocks and token-shaped strings out of the repository text itself (`tests/Contract/ServerContractTest.php:101-110`).

A reviewer can check the channels by reading `tests/Security/EnvAndRedactionTest.php` and the audit-log writer, and by running `composer test`.

### What is left [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/data-exfiltration.html#what-is-left)

The redactor is pattern-based and blunt on purpose: a false positive costs a word, a miss costs a key (`src/Security/Redactor.php:7-11`). The patterns cover the shapes developers actually leak; they are not a general-purpose secret scanner. A secret that matches no known shape, such as an unusual variable name or a quoted value with no key, passes through.

Files inside the project root remain readable by the child programs and quotable in their output; confinement decides where, not what. The environment allowlist is a whitelist of names, not values: an allowed name such as `PATH` is passed through untouched.

Once a value reaches the model's context, the client's own logging, retention and network behavior decide the rest, which is outside ADVISOR's control. The audit log helps a developer spot an odd call after the fact, but it hashes the arguments rather than hiding them from the model, which already saw them.

---

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html

## Path traversal [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html#path-traversal)

An attacker who controls a tool's path argument wants to read files outside the project: private keys, credentials, neighboring projects, or enough of the disk layout to plan a next step.

### Where it applies in ADVISOR [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html#where-it-applies-in-advisor)

Two tools take a `path` argument, and both hand the resolved folder to a child program:

- `run_proctor_check` runs the app's own PROCTOR on the given folder; the schema says the path must be inside the project root (`src/Tools/RunProctorCheck.php:30`).
- `upgrade_path` runs Booster's read-only `plan` on the given folder, with the same constraint (`src/Tools/UpgradePath.php:31`).

Both default to the project root itself, so even a call with no arguments goes through the guard. The guard's root comes from `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT` and is fixed once when the server starts (`src/Server/Runtime.php:44`); nothing a model sends can move it.

The schema caps the argument at 1024 characters, the same limit the guard enforces (`src/Tools/RunProctorCheck.php:30`, `src/Tools/UpgradePath.php:31`).

PROCTOR and BOOSTER read whatever sits under the folder they are given, so that folder is the only boundary between their file access and the rest of the machine. The other tools take no path at all: `read_project_docs` takes a project id and a document name from closed lists (`src/Tools/ReadProjectDocs.php:27-28`), and the rest take no file input.

### What stops it [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html#what-stops-it)

- **Odd input is refused before resolution.** Empty paths, paths over 1024 characters and null bytes are rejected (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:40-42`), as are paths that start with `~` (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:43-45`).
- **Parent segments are refused outright.** Any segment equal to `..`, under forward or back slashes, ends the call (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:46-50`).
- **Resolution follows symlinks, then checks containment.** The path is resolved to its real location and must sit inside the resolved root (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:52-57`), so a symlink inside the project that points out of it fails the same way `../../` does.
- **Missing and outside get the same error**, so a refusal does not map the disk for the attacker (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:54-56`).
- **Prefix tricks fail.** Containment compares against the root plus a separator, so a sibling folder whose name merely starts with the root's is refused (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:70`), and on Windows the comparison is case-insensitive (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:65-68`).
- **Drive-letter roots are handled.** Absolute-path detection covers `/`, `\` and `C:` style roots, so a Windows absolute path cannot slip past the prefix check (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:83-86`).
- **The root itself is validated.** The constructor refuses a root that is not a directory, so the guard cannot be pointed at a file (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:21-28`).
- **Output never shows the host layout.** Paths in results are rendered relative to the project root (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:73-80`, used at `src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:127` and `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:140`).

The tests prove each refusal: hostile paths covering `..` segments, nested and backslash parents, `~`, null bytes, absolute paths elsewhere, missing files and overlong strings (`tests/Security/PathGuardTest.php:43-63`); a same-prefix sibling folder (`tests/Security/PathGuardTest.php:65-72`); a symlink that leaves the project (`tests/Security/PathGuardTest.php:74-82`); and errors that never show the host layout (`tests/Security/PathGuardTest.php:84-92`). The contract test adds that no tool may be named like a shell command or take a free-form command, cmd, script, code, sql or url argument at all (`tests/Contract/ServerContractTest.php:59-68`).

The same two tools are the only ones that start a process; see [Command injection](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/command-injection.html) for how their argument lists are pinned.

### What is left [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/path-traversal.html#what-is-left)

Confinement is to the configured project root, and everything inside that root is readable by these tools by design, since they exist to inspect the app. The guard checks the path once per call; a symlink swapped in after the check, before PROCTOR or BOOSTER reads the file, is not caught, and a path that moves out later (a bind mount, a moved volume) is outside the guard's view.

The guard also trusts the root it is given (`src/Security/PathGuard.php:21-28`): pointing `ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT` at a wide folder is an operator decision, and the guard will faithfully confine to it. Because the child programs run with normal file access inside the root, the guard decides where they may look, not what they may do with what they find.

---

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html

## Prompt injection [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html#prompt-injection)

An attacker who controls some of the text ADVISOR serves wants the model reading that text to follow hidden instructions, leak data, or trust a false answer.

### Where it applies in ADVISOR [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html#where-it-applies-in-advisor)

Every tool result is plain text that lands in the client model's context, so anything ADVISOR serves is a possible carrier for instructions aimed at the model:

- `read_project_docs` serves bundled READMEs, best-practices guides and migration notes from the stack repositories (`src/Tools/ReadProjectDocs.php:23`).
- `list_stack_rules` serves CREED handbook text, rule by rule (`src/Tools/ListStackRules.php:70-78`).
- `run_proctor_check` returns finding messages that quote the project's own files (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:116`).
- `upgrade_path` returns plan steps and warnings that come from the app's manifests (`src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:209`).
- Tool descriptions, resources and prompts are also text the client reads before any call is made.

The interesting cases are the ones the developer never typed: a document shipped in a stack repository, or a file inside the project that PROCTOR quotes back. Both reach the model inside an answer that looks like a trusted reference, which is exactly what makes them persuasive. The resources (the policy feed, the CREED chapter feeds and the guide feeds) serve the same hash-pinned content as the tools (`src/Module/CoreModule.php:52-83`).

### What stops it [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html#what-stops-it)

- **Answers are labeled as data.** Every result carries its `source` and a `generated_on` date, and the docs tool says outright that the text is reference material, not instructions (`src/Tools/ReadProjectDocs.php:63-64`, `src/Tools/ReadProjectDocs.php:68`). The rules tool repeats the point (`src/Tools/ListStackRules.php:76`).
- **Decisions stay with PROCTOR.** PROCTOR reports say PROCTOR in CI decides pass or fail (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:131`), and Booster plans say they change nothing (`src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:180`), so a served answer cannot claim authority it does not have.
- **Invisible characters are stripped and rejected.** Zero-width, bidirectional and TAG-block controls can hide instructions from a human reviewer. They are removed from child-process output before it is served (`src/Security/ProctorRunner.php:82`, `src/Security/BoosterRunner.php:209`) and refused in bundled content at start-up (`src/Content/ContentBundle.php:98-101`).
- **The published surface is scanned.** Tools, resources and prompts are checked for hidden characters on every test run (`tests/Contract/ServerContractTest.php:70-79`), as are the shipped prompt files themselves (`tests/Contract/ServerContractTest.php:80-82`).
- **Bundled content is hash-pinned.** Every file under `data/` must match its SHA-256 manifest hash or the server throws at start-up (`src/Content/ContentBundle.php:51-58`, `src/Content/ContentBundle.php:95-97`), so a served document cannot change between release and use.
- **Tool metadata is snapshotted.** A quiet change to a tool name or description (tool poisoning) fails the snapshot test instead of shipping unnoticed (`tests/Server/McpServerTest.php:121-138`).
- **ADVISOR talks to no one.** It makes no network calls and no model calls of its own (`docs/guides/safety.md:19`), so there is no second channel for served text to act through.

The layers are deliberate: labeling tells the model what the text is, pinning keeps it stable, stripping removes the hidden channels, and the snapshot test makes quiet changes loud.

A reviewer can check these controls without trusting this page: read the `notice` fields above, run `composer ci` (the contract and snapshot tests are part of it), and diff `tools/list` against the committed snapshot.

### What is left [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/threats/prompt-injection.html#what-is-left)

Labels reduce the risk, but they do not make injected instructions inert. A client model can still be fooled by text it reads, especially text that quotes the project's own files in the middle of a plausible report, and ADVISOR's job is to make sure that text is labeled, pinned and clean, not to guarantee the model will ignore it.

Hash pinning guarantees the text is what was released, not that it is harmless: a compromised upstream repository could ship a malicious document, and the manifest would bless it. Stripping invisible characters catches the sneaky encodings, not the plain-language ones. Nothing in ADVISOR can tell a well-written instruction from a well-written report. The client's own defenses, and the developer's review of what the model does with the text, are the last line.

---

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html

## Troubleshooting [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

This page lists the failure symptoms ADVISOR's own docs describe, with the cause, the fix and the command that checks it.

### The advisor server is not in the list [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-advisor-server-is-not-in-the-list)

You added the config, opened the project, and the `advisor` server is not in the list.

**Cause.** One of four things keeps a server from appearing:

- **php**: the PHP on your machine satisfies ADVISOR's own `composer.json` (8.3 or newer).
- **content**: the bundled `data/` still matches its manifest.
- **client:claude**, **client:warriorgpt**, **client:cursor**, **client:vscode**: each client's MCP config: is the file there, does it have the `advisor` entry, and is the script it points at in the project? A missing file is a warning, not a failure; you only need the one client you use.
- **mcp**: the server actually starts. Doctor boots it in-process and asks for its tools.

**Fix.** Run doctor and fix anything it reports as a `fail`. A `fail` is something to fix; a `warn` is something you may not care about.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

The exit code is `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did; `--json` prints the findings as JSON.

### The server refuses to start because it is not enabled [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-server-refuses-to-start-because-it-is-not-enabled)

**Cause.** `ADVISOR_ENABLED` defaults to off. It must be `1` or `true`, or the server refuses to start.

**Fix.** Set `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in the client config's environment. `advisor install` sets it in the client config.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

### The server refuses to start in production [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-server-refuses-to-start-in-production)

**Cause.** `ADVISOR_ENV` reads `APP_ENV`, then `local`. `production` or `prod` always refuses to start.

**Fix.** Run ADVISOR in development only. It refuses to start in production by design.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

### A bad setting stops the server [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-bad-setting-stops-the-server)

**Cause.** A bad value stops the server with a message on stderr. It does not guess.

**Fix.** Read the message on stderr and correct the value. ADVISOR reads the process environment only, never a file.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

### The server refuses to start because a content file fails its hash [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-server-refuses-to-start-because-a-content-file-fails-its-hash)

**Cause.** The bundled `data/` is verified at start-up against `data/manifest.json` (a SHA-256 for every file). If a file does not match, the server refuses to start rather than serve it.

**Fix.** Regenerate the bundle from the sibling stack repositories with `content:generate`, then verify it.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify
```

### Related [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#related)

## Upgrading [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page walks through each released version of ADVISOR and what changed, so you can see whether a new version affects your app.

### \[0.3.0\] - 2026-11-09 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-0-2026-11-09)

A new minor line, so a `^0.2` constraint does not pick it up: move to `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.3`. No code in your app changes; the MCP server reports version 0.3.0.

- The parts list has fifteen projects: Parity, Citadel on your own computer, comes after Squire. `get_project_status` and `read_project_docs` take `parity`, so an agent that validates project ids against the tool's enum sees one more.
- `owner_of` answers "local development" with Parity, and the deploy-files row no longer lists the parity kit under Squire.
- A project whose `CHANGELOG.md` heading says unreleased no longer shows that number as its version, and a Go module counts as built.
- The bundled data is resynced with the stack's 2026-11-09 night main branches, and the front page deploy layer runs Squire's kit 0.10.2 with CREED ^0.1.8 and HELMET ^1.3.

### \[0.2.0\] - 2026-11-09 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-0-2026-11-09)

A new minor line, so a `^0.1` constraint does not pick it up: move to `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.2`. ADVISOR now requires `waynestate/creed` (^0.1.8); if your app locks an older CREED (PROCTOR brings one), let Composer move it too with `composer update waynestate/advisor --with-dependencies`. The MCP server reports version 0.2.0.

- `policy_lookup` and `get_project_status` answer through CREED's own reader, so they say exactly what PROCTOR decides. A line the policy marks current (Vue 3, Inertia 2 and 3) now reads `active` instead of having no state, and a version older than every line the policy lists is answered as end of life with a note instead of being refused.
- `upgrade_path` takes `from_php`, for a project whose `composer.json` names no PHP constraint (Booster's `--from-php`).
- Only for module authors: `ContentBundle::policy()` returns CREED's `Waynestate\Creed\Policy`, `Content\PolicyReader` only checks the schema version, and `Content\State` is gone (use `Waynestate\Creed\State`). No stack project ships a module yet.
- The bundled data is resynced with the stack's 2026-11-09 main branches, the docs gain four threat pages, and the front page deploy layer runs Squire's kit 0.10.1 with HELMET ^1.0 and PROCTOR ^0.11.

### \[0.1.7\] - 2026-11-07 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-7-2026-11-07)

No breaking changes are marked for this release. Update with `composer update waynestate/advisor`; the MCP server reports version 0.1.7.

- `owner_of` answers from an ownership table rebuilt from the stack's decisions, and `read_project_docs` trims image boilerplate at read time as well.
- The bundled data is resynced with the stack's 2026-11-07 releases, and the canonical repository is git.wayne.edu.

### \[0.1.6\] - 2026-11-06 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-6-2026-11-06)

No breaking changes are marked for this release. Update with `composer update waynestate/advisor`; the MCP server reports version 0.1.6.

- symfony/console and symfony/process accept ^8.0 as well as ^7.4, so apps on Pest 5 / PHPUnit 13 can install ADVISOR.
- The bundled data is resynced with the stack's main branches through the evening of 2026-11-06, including Booster 1.9.0, WELD 0.1.3, the accessibility gates across the stack and the Sourdough raw PHP + Vue shape.
- A docs site built from `docs/` is added and checked in `composer ci`, and the front page and docs pass an accessibility gate. The proof runner is dev tooling and is not part of the served product.

### \[0.1.5\] - 2026-11-03 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-5-2026-11-03)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- The deploy layer requires HELMET ^0.3 and PROCTOR ^0.4 (locked at 0.3.0 and 0.4.0) and sets minimum-stability to stable, which clears PROCTOR 0.4's new minimum-stability warning. HELMET 0.3 reads an empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` as trust nobody; the front page sets only the `citadel` preset, so nothing changes for it.
- The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.5.0 (updated `base-fallback.Dockerfile`, `scripts/release.sh` and `scripts/parity.ps1`).
- The bundled data is resynced with the 2026-11-03 releases: Booster 1.8.0, Preflight 0.1.4, PROCTOR 0.4.0, Pinstripe 0.1.2, CREED 0.1.6, Rollcall 0.1.9, HELMET 0.3.0, SESAME 0.4.0, Drawbridge 0.1.1, Sourdough 0.1.5, Squire 0.5.0 and WELD 0.1.2, and with each project's main since the last pass.
- One Playbook settings resolver (`Waynestate\Advisor\Playbook\Settings`, ADR-0018) is added. `playbook_lookup` now answers from `.env.playbook` when the package is not installed (same output shape).
- `.env.playbook` is git-ignored; the agent-ready files (`site/llms.txt`, `site/llms-full.txt`) are regenerated.
- Docs and package metadata name nougat as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.

### \[0.1.4\] - 2026-11-03 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-4-2026-11-03)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit.

### \[0.1.3\] - 2026-11-02 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-3-2026-11-02)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- Hand-written guides are bundled from `generator/guides/` and served as `advisor://guide/<slug>`; the first guide is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel".
- `policy_lookup` returns `latest_patch`; the bundled docs drop hero images, badges and GIFs.
- WayneUI's migration guide (MIGRATING.md) is bundled as the `migrating` doc, and every project entry carries its version when it publishes one (composer.json, else package.json, else the newest CHANGELOG heading).
- A one-line `claude mcp add` and a Docker `.mcp.json` for machines without PHP are documented.
- `composer content:drift` and an optional CI job fail when `data/` no longer matches the sibling repos.
- The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local `.env.squire` file is now git-ignored).

### \[0.1.2\] - 2026-10-29 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-2-2026-10-29)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- An agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt) is added from Squire's kit.
- The `playbook_lookup` tool answers "what is the value of X?" for WSU shared values. An environment variable of the same name wins, then the private `waynestate/playbook` package (Playbook) supplies the rest; without it the tool says how to get it instead of failing. Keys that look like secrets (ending in SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN or KEY) are refused. `waynestate/playbook` is suggested, never required.
- Docs copies are resynced; proof results now live on the proof site.
- Project names are written as words except acronyms.
- Stale capability claims in the site and docs are fixed.

### \[0.1.1\] - 2026-10-29 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- The `owner_of` tool answers "which project owns X?" from a new bundled `data/ownership.json` table (sourced from `generator/ownership.json`, verified by `content:verify`). Fuzzy match: every word of the topic must appear in a row's topic or role; a no-match answer lists every known topic.
- `upgrade_path` moves from the `stack` group to a new `booster` group, so `ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack` offers reference tools only and never starts a program. `ADVISOR_GROUPS` now accepts `stack`, `proctor` and `booster`.
- PHPStan includes Pinstripe's `raw.neon` preset (`waynestate/pinstripe` 0.1.0 as a dev dependency) instead of a hand copy of its settings; two docblocks were tightened to satisfy the preset's method-signature checks. Pint already used the `per` preset, so `pint.json` is unchanged.

### \[0.1.0\] - 2026-10-29 [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0-2026-10-29)

This is the first release, so there is nothing to break.

- Read-only MCP server over stdio (`php vendor/bin/advisor mcp`) on the official `mcp/sdk` 0.9.0, speaking both the legacy `initialize` handshake and the 2026-07-28 per-request form.
- Seven tools: `list_projects`, `get_project_status`, `read_project_docs`, `policy_lookup`, `list_stack_rules`, `run_proctor_check`, `upgrade_path`. Resources `advisor://policy` and `advisor://creed/<chapter>`. Prompts `orient_me` and `plan_upgrade`.
- `upgrade_path` plans the app's PHP and/or Laravel upgrade, one supported hop at a time, by running Booster's read-only `plan` (never `run`) against the bundled policy. New settings `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_TIMEOUT` (default 60) and `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN` (fallback when the app has no `vendor/bin/booster` of its own).
- Bundled, hash-verified content (CREED handbook and policy, project docs, the WayneUI markup contract) with a generator, `content:generate --check` and `content:verify`.
- `advisor install` for Claude, WarriorGPT, Cursor, VS Code (written) and Codex (printed).
- Laravel adapter on `laravel/mcp` (`php artisan mcp:start advisor`), so ADVISOR runs beside Laravel Boost.
- Safety: off unless enabled, refuses production, read-only by default, path confinement, allowlisted child environment, redaction, invisible-character stripping, manifest-only module loading, argument-hash audit log.
- `composer ci`: validate, content verify, PHPUnit, Pint, PHPStan level 8 (Pinstripe settings), audit. CI files for GitLab (Preflight 0.1.0) and GitHub.

### Taking a new version [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#taking-a-new-version)

ADVISOR is on Packagist: `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.3`. No extra repository needed.

The command is then `php vendor/bin/advisor`. This works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, because it is one PHP command and not a shell script.
